entries.title: THE THIRTEENTH WOLF
entries.notes: Current blurb was a generic guess from the title. Originally a 68 minute Black Library audio drama, November 2016, so type corrected from Short Story to Audio Drama. Thousand Sons added as a featured faction (traitor Legion, and a genuine change to the faction filter). Editor Laurie Goulding places it 'immediately after A Thousand Sons'. Timeline left at 004-005.M31 to match PROSPERO BURNS, though the Battle of Prospero itself is dated 734.004.M31, so 004.M31 would be slightly more precise.

entries.title: INTO EXILE
entries.notes: The prior audit was right. This has nothing to do with the Word Bearers. Legions corrected from Word Bearers (traitor) to Mechanicum and Imperial Fists (loyalist), which flips the loyalist/traitor filter. Type Short Story confirmed (Black Library Advent Calendar 2016, day three). Timeline narrowed from 005-007.M31 to 005-006.M31, the span of the Schism of Mars, since Goulding places it 'immediately after Mechanicum'. It is a prequel to THE MASTER OF MANKIND and leads into the webway arc.

entries.title: CYBERNETICA
entries.notes: Not a story about battle-automata as the current blurb assumed. Originally a 128 page limited edition novella, December 2015, so type corrected from Short Story to Novella. Raven Guard and Imperial Fists added alongside Mechanicum, both loyalist, so no traitor flip. Timeline 005.M31 kept and confirmed, the Schism of Mars runs 005-006.M31 and the Terra framing scenes sit at the later end of that.

entries.title: THE BINARY SUCCESSION
entries.notes: Type corrected from Novella to Audio Drama (75 minutes, nine voice actors, March 2017). Legions Mechanicum confirmed. The big change is the date. Goulding places it 'soon before The Master of Mankind', which this database dates 011.M31, so 006.M31 is far too early. Set to 010-011.M31, flagged medium confidence because no source gives an exact Imperial date. Track of Words also notes Goulding's later story THE LAST COUNCIL sits between this and THE SOLAR WAR, which supports a late placement. The current blurb wrongly implies fighting on Mars, the action is political and set on Terra.

entries.title: PERPETUAL
entries.notes: Type corrected from Novella to Audio Drama (27 minutes, Advent Calendar 2016 day one). Timeline 007.M31 and faction Perpetuals both confirmed, Goulding places it after MARK OF CALTH. Main characters trimmed: the site currently lists John Grammaticus, but neither the Black Library synopsis nor the Track of Words review places him with Oll's band here, and the wiki has Grammaticus held elsewhere by Prytanis during this period. Removing him is medium confidence, the rest is high.

entries.title: ORDO SINISTER
entries.notes: Type Short Story confirmed (digital only, February 2017). Faction Collegia Titanica confirmed. The current blurb is wrong in substance: this is the War Within the Webway, not the defence of Terra or the coming Siege, and it is one Titan rather than 'the Psi-Titans' plural. Timeline moved from 007.M31 to 011.M31 because Goulding places it 'immediately before The Master of Mankind', which this database dates 011.M31. Medium confidence on the exact date as no source gives an Imperial dating.

entries.title: THE WOLF KING
entries.notes: The prior audit was right on all counts. Type corrected from Short Story to Novella (128 page limited edition, October 2015). Alpha Legion added, which puts a traitor Legion on this entry for the first time, plus Dark Angels for the contingent that intervenes. Timeline 007.M31 confirmed by the Battle of the Alaxxes Nebula, so the audit's 'roughly 007.M31' matches what is already recorded. Black Library titles the novella 'Wolf King' without the definite article, the site title was left as is to avoid breaking keys.

entries.title: THE HEART OF THE PHAROS
entries.notes: The prior audit was right that this concerns the Pharos on Sotha, but the current blurb's 'corrupts those who seek to control it' is invention. Type corrected from Short Story to Audio Drama (38 minutes, February 2016, originally announced as 'The Dark Between the Stars'). Timeline 009.M31 and faction Ultramarines both confirmed, it sits between THE UNREMEMBERED EMPIRE and PHAROS. Barabas Dantioch features, but Iron Warriors was deliberately not added to legions because he is a loyalist and the tag would wrongly trip the traitor filter. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: WEREGELD
entries.notes: The current text was fabricated: Weregeld is not the start of a quest for vengeance after Isstvan, it is the closing novella of the Corax arc, new to the Book 40 anthology in 2016. Setting is the Battle of Yarant III, which follows Leman Russ's wounding by Horus at Trisolian (Wolfsbane) and sits alongside the Beta-Garmon campaign, so 013.M31 rather than 006-007.M31. Corax explicitly dispatches non-Raven Guard elements to Terra and Beta-Garmon during the story, which anchors the late date. Date is a reasoned placement, not a printed in-universe stamp, so treat as approximate. Ordering: this should be the LAST Corax entry, not the first. The site currently numbers it XL.1.

entries.title: SOULFORGE
entries.notes: The prior audit was right. The current text described the plot of Deliverance Lost (obtaining gene-tech from Terra to rebuild the Legion). Soulforge is the 2013 Limited Edition novella set after Deliverance Lost, and is the assault on the forge world Constanix II. Word Bearers and the Dark Mechanicum are the antagonists and must be added to the factions. Type and timeline confirmed unchanged.

entries.title: RAVENLORD
entries.notes: The current text was fabricated: Ravenlord is not about destroying failed gene-seed creations (that is the Ravendelve disaster at the end of Deliverance Lost). It is the 2014 Limited Edition novella covering the assault on the prison colony Carandiru. Type and timeline unchanged. Ordering caveat: Lexicanum and the Warhammer 40k Wiki both place Ravenlord THIRD in the Raven Guard chronology (Soulforge, The Shadowmasters, Ravenlord, The Value of Fear, Raptor, Weregeld), not fifth. I could not find a source supporting the fifth position.

entries.title: THE SHADOWMASTERS
entries.notes: Type confirmed as Short Story: first published inside the dust jacket of the Corax: Soulforge hardback, later also issued as an audio book (April 2015) and collected in Book 40. Because it depicts an engagement concurrent with Soulforge, the timeline is narrowed from 007-008.M31 to 007.M31. Track of Words names the theatre as 'Atlas'; I could not independently confirm whether Atlas is a location on or near Constanix II, so the blurb refers to the wider Legion assault rather than naming it. Confidence medium on setting detail only, high on protagonist and premise.

entries.title: GARRO: OATH OF MOMENT
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (2010, Toby Longworth, roughly 71 minutes). The current text was generic and omitted the entire actual plot, Calth and Rubio. Timeline 007.M31 retained as consistent with the Battle of Calth. The 'greenskin invasion' in the official blurb is the pretext for the Calth muster, not the real enemy.

entries.title: GARRO: SWORD OF TRUTH
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (2012, roughly 140 minutes, John Banks, Toby Longworth, Ramon Tikaram). Current text was generic and wrong in emphasis: Garro is not hunting loyalists inside traitor Legions, he is vetting a mixed loyalist-claiming flotilla at the edge of the Solar System. One contingent is a traitor plant; secondary sources name the White Scars captain Hakeem, but I only found this in aggregated wiki snippets so I have deliberately kept the identity out of the blurb. Ordering evidence: the official blurb states Garro 'returns from the battlefields of Calth', and Macer Varren is recruited here but is already a Knight-Errant in Legion of One, so Sword of Truth precedes Legion of One chronologically. The site's order is correct on this point.

entries.title: THE VALUE OF FEAR
entries.notes: The current text simply restated the title as a theme. The actual story is a Raven Guard and loyalist Night Lords joint action in an underhive, from the Black Library 2014 Advent Calendar (roughly 1,000 words). Night Lords must be added to the factions; the official blurb names them explicitly. The Alpha Legion role in the rebellion comes from the Track of Words review only, so it is the least certain element. Type Short Story and timeline 008.M31 unchanged.

entries.title: RAPTOR
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (March 2015, 69 minutes, cast including Joe Absolom and Sean Barrett), though the Corax anthology reprints it as prose and Black Library's contents listing labels it a short story. The current text was wrong on the central fact: the Raptors are already mutated when the story opens, they do not transform into monsters at the end. Space Wolves must be added to the factions. Timeline 008.M31 unchanged, no printed in-universe date found.

entries.title: GARRO: LEGION OF ONE
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (2011, 68 minutes, Toby Longworth). Current text was pure title-paraphrase and factually wrong: Garro is not alone, he is one of three Knights-Errant. Legions added for Rubio (Ultramarines), Varren (World Eaters) and Loken (Luna Wolves, listed as Sons of Horus). Timeline left at 008.M31 but flagged: the official blurb says 'almost a year' after Isstvan III, which would sit earlier, while the story must post-date Sword of Truth because Varren is already a Knight-Errant. The published canon is loose here and I found no printed in-universe date.

entries.title: GARRO: SHIELD OF LIES
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (130 minutes, cast including Jonathan Keeble and Toby Longworth). Current text was a title-paraphrase with no real content; the actual story is largely told from Tallery's viewpoint on the orbital plate Riga. Mechanicum added as the pursuing force. Timeline 008-009.M31 retained, no printed in-universe date found.

entries.title: BURDEN OF DUTY
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (October 2012, John Banks, Toby Longworth, Ramon Tikaram; later re-released on CD alongside Grey Angel). Current text was generic sentiment with no plot. Imperial Fists added. Lexicanum also states that Massak declines to leave with Garro; I found that in only one source chain so I have left the outcome out of the blurb rather than assert it. Black Library now titles the story 'Garro: Burden of Duty'; the original 2012 release was 'Burden of Duty', which is what the manifest uses. Timeline 009-010.M31 retained, no printed in-universe date found.

entries.title: GARRO: ASHES OF FEALTY
entries.notes: Type Audio Drama confirmed (2015, 18 minutes, Jonathan Keeble and Toby Longworth). Current text was a title-paraphrase about loyalty; the actual story is the reunion with Meric Voyen and his search for a cure to the Death Guard's affliction. Death Guard added to factions. Timeline 010-011.M31 retained, no printed in-universe date found.

entries.title: GARRO: VOW OF FAITH
entries.notes: Type Novella confirmed (December 2015 limited edition hardback plus simultaneous ebook; the only non-audio original in the Garro collection). The current text overreached badly, claiming Garro founds the Grey Knights and the Inquisition; nothing of the sort happens here. The story is his crisis of faith and his search for Euphrati Keeler on Terra. Timeline 011-013.M31 retained, no printed in-universe date found.

entries.title: THE WOLF OF ASH AND FIRE
entries.notes: The Space Wolves attribution was wrong, a title guess. This is the XVI Legion under their pre-Heresy name of Luna Wolves, fighting orks on Gorro with the Emperor present. Originally an exclusive attached to the Macragge's Honour graphic novel. Hastur Sejanus is listed per the audit brief plus Track of Words noting Mournival dialogue, but Lexicanum does not name him, so treat that one name as slightly weaker than the rest.

entries.title: AURELIAN
entries.notes: The existing entry was broadly right, unusually for this batch. Sharpened with the actual frame story, four days after the Isstvan V Drop Site Massacre, and the named daemon guide Ingethel. Added Chaos Daemons to the faction list since An'ggrath, Kairos Fateweaver and Ingethel all appear. Format Novella confirmed, originally a 2011 limited hardback.

entries.title: THE LONG NIGHT
entries.notes: Confirms the audit brief. Sevatar is imprisoned aboard the Invincible Reason, so the Dark Angels belong in the faction list alongside the Night Lords. Timeline of 009.M31 verified against the Thramas Crusade, dated 007 to 009.M31 and ended at Sheol IX. Format kept as Audio Drama, the original November 2014 release, though the anthology carries the prose adaptation.

entries.title: MASSACRE
entries.notes: Legions was listed as Various, which is wrong. This is squarely a Night Lords story, First Claw at the Isstvan V Drop Site Massacre, hence 006.M31. The author's own site describes it as First Claw fighting through the Dropsite Massacre in vignettes.

entries.title: BROTHERHOOD OF THE MOON
entries.notes: White Scars was already correct, but the blurb was generic filler. The actual content is Torghun Khan's trial after the Legion's internal rebellion, tied to Scars. Timeline of 007.M31 left as is and is consistent with Scars, though Lexicanum gives no explicit date.

entries.title: INHERITOR
entries.notes: Serious error corrected. The entry was tagged Dark Angels, presumably because Gav Thorpe writes the Dark Angels. It is in fact a Word Bearers story, Torquill Eliphas of the Ark of Testimony Chapter on Kronus, with World Eaters allies against Ultramarines defenders. This flips the entry from loyalist to traitor.

entries.title: VORAX
entries.notes: Faction corrected from the vague Mechanicum to Dark Mechanicum plus the blockading Imperial Fists. Lexicanum carries only the Black Library cover copy and no character names, so mainCharacters is deliberately empty and the blurb stays at the level the source supports rather than inventing a protagonist. The 005-006.M31 date is unverified, the Imperial Fists blockade of the Ring of Iron follows the Schism of Mars, so it may sit slightly later.

entries.title: IRONFIRE
entries.notes: Serious error corrected. Iron Hands was a title guess. This is Iron Warriors, Warsmith Idriss Krendl on Euphorus, a direct sequel to The Iron Within, exactly as the audit flagged. Flips the entry from loyalist to traitor. One review, Adventures with Peps, states the palace is held by Emperor's Children, and Track of Words hints at a traitor-against-traitor dynamic, but I could not corroborate the defenders from a second solid source, so I left them out of the faction list and out of the blurb.

entries.title: RED-MARKED
entries.notes: Legions was Various, which is wrong. This is an Ultramarines story starring Aeonid Thiel, set after Calth and the Shadow Crusade with Word Bearers remnants as the threat. The 007.M31 date is left unchanged but is questionable, the source places it during Imperium Secundus, which argues for 008 or 009.M31 and would sit close to Stratagem.

entries.title: MASTER OF THE FIRST
entries.notes: Dark Angels was already correct, as the audit expected, but the old blurb invented a Deathwing angle that has nothing to do with the story. It is set on Caliban and concerns Astelan, Luther and a failed coup. Timeline of 007-009.M31 is consistent with the Thramas Crusade and left unchanged.

entries.title: STRATAGEM
entries.notes: Legions was Various. It is an Ultramarines piece, Thiel and Guilliman, and it is the in-universe origin of the Codex-era stratagem concept. Originally a 2014 Advent Calendar audio drama, 21 minutes.

entries.title: SINS OF THE FATHER
entries.notes: Blood Angels was correct but everything else was generic gene-seed-curse filler. The actual content is the Azkaellon versus Amit ritual duel. Format changed from Short Story to Audio Drama, Lexicanum records it as an Andy Smillie audio drama published 17 November 2014, 13 minutes, performed by Toby Longworth, Jonathan Keeble and Steve Conlin, with a prose version following later, which is what the anthology carries. The 001.M31 timeline could not be verified from any source and is left untouched rather than guessed at.

entries.title: HERALD OF SANGUINIUS
entries.notes: Blood Angels correct. The old blurb invented a messenger carrying word from Sanguinius, which is a title guess. The story is actually about Sanguinius on the throne of Imperium Secundus and Azkaellon's Sanguinary Guard countering an internal threat. Originally a December 2014 Advent Calendar audio drama, 20 minutes.

entries.title: THE EAGLE'S TALON
entries.notes: Serious error corrected. Emperor's Children was wrong. This is Imperial Fists against Iron Warriors at Tallarn, as the audit flagged, which flips the entry from traitor to loyalist. The 010-011.M31 date is now positively confirmed against the Battle of Tallarn article rather than merely assumed.

entries.title: IRON CORPSES
entries.notes: Serious error corrected. Iron Hands was a title guess. This is Iron Warriors, Warsmith Koparnos, and it is a direct sequel to The Eagle's Talon on Tallarn. Flips the entry from loyalist to traitor. Collegia Titanica added for the loyalist Titan and its princeps, Benwrath, though the source does not name her Legio. Date confirmed against the Battle of Tallarn.

entries.title: THE FINAL COMPLIANCE OF SIXTY-THREE FOURTEEN
entries.notes: Legions changed from Various to Sons of Horus, the XVI Legion, which both sources agree on. No source I could reach names a protagonist, so mainCharacters is left empty and the blurb stays within what the Black Library cover copy and the Grimdark Archive entry support. The 006.M31 date is plausible for a post-Isstvan reconquest sweep but is not stated anywhere I could verify.

entries.title: MYRIAD
entries.notes: Manifest was badly wrong: no Alpha Legion content at all. This is a Mars/Mechanicum story, a direct sequel to Rob Sanders's novella Cybernetica, released 19 August 2016 as Day 5 of the Summer of Reading. Protagonist is a human ex-princeps, not a Space Marine. Timeline confidence is LOW and is a bracket, not a sourced year: no source gives a date, so the range spans the Imperial blockade of Mars (Lexicanum: Mars blockaded 006-015.M31) up to the eve of the Siege. The blanket 012-013.M31 is certainly wrong for a mid-war Martian insurgency story. Legion names Legio Vendettica etc. appear but the loyalist/traitor axis here is Mechanicum vs Dark Mechanicum.

entries.title: THE GREY RAVEN
entries.notes: Legion was already correct, so only dating and content changed. Published 7 December 2016 as Day 7 of Advent 2016; Lexicanum lists Weregeld as the preceding work. Dated 012.M31 because Corax dispatches Kurthuri to Terra at the same juncture that he takes the Legion to the Battle of Yarant, which Lexicanum dates 012.M31. Deliberately did not name the Imperial Fists and Custodes escort (Noriz, Arcatus) in the blurb: Lexicanum attributes that detail to Kurthuri's wider biography rather than unambiguously to this story, so legions is left as Raven Guard only.

entries.title: VALERIUS
entries.notes: Format confirmed as Audio Drama (Day 16 of Advent 2016, performed by Gareth Armstrong, John Banks and others). Protagonist is a mortal Imperial Army officer, not a Space Marine, so 'Various' was replaced with Imperial Army plus Raven Guard, the Therion Cohort being the Raven Guard's attached Army formation and Corax being the one who sends him. Timeline retains 012-013.M31 but this is now genuinely derived rather than blanket: Lexicanum dates the second phase of the Battle of Beta-Garmon to 012-013.M31, and Valerius's banishment follows the Battle of Yarant (012.M31).

entries.title: THE EMBER WOLVES
entries.notes: Serious faction error corrected: there are no Space Wolves in this story. The Ember Wolves are the Legio Audax, a TRAITOR Titan Legion long associated with the World Eaters, so the manifest's Space Wolves tag would have flipped this from traitor to loyalist on the site. Released online March 2017 as part of the 'March of the Titans' promotion; format is an e-short, i.e. Short Story, which the manifest already had right. TIMELINE UNRESOLVED: no source gives a year, so the blanket 012-013.M31 is retained as a placeholder rather than as a finding. Note Lexicanum's Legio Audax page files an Absalom engagement under the Great Crusade in M30 where the Audax fight ALONGSIDE Tantorus Magnificat, which is most likely the flashback inside this story rather than its present-day setting; the Legio Castigatra page cites this story for the Heresy-era Battle of Absolom in which Tantorus is destroyed. Princeps Balthus Voltemand is sourced only from the Track of Words review, as Lexicanum has no page for him.

entries.title: BLACKSHIELD
entries.notes: Manifest tagged this generically as Blackshields; the viewpoint character is in fact a Death Guard, so both factions are now listed. Released 15 August 2016 as Day 1 of the 2016 Summer of Reading. Timeline is a derived bracket, not a quoted year: Khorak defects after the Battle of Molech, which Lexicanum dates 009.M31, and Morturg resolves at the story's end to return to Terra, which places it comfortably before the Siege. Confidence high on content, medium on the exact years.

entries.title: CHILDREN OF SICARUS
entries.notes: Manifest had the Legion right but the plot wrong: this is not Word Bearers marching on Terra. It is Kor Phaeron marooned in the Eye of Terror, and it establishes how Sicarus became the Word Bearers' homeworld. Format confirmed Audio Drama, released October 2016, 39 minutes, performed by Gareth Armstrong, John Banks, Tim Bentinck and others. Timeline 007.M31 is derived: Lexicanum dates the Battle of Calth to 007.M31 and this picks up directly from the graphic novel Macragge's Honour, which is the pursuit immediately after Calth. Caveat, and why confidence is medium: the story covers an unspecified stretch of time on Sicarus and Jepeth's prophecy looks forward to the Siege, so the later part may run past 007.M31.

entries.title: EXOCYTOSIS
entries.notes: Main correction is the missing Dark Angels: this is a two-Legion story, Typhon as guest and Luther's Fallen as wary hosts, and the tension comes from their contrasting outlooks. Published 20 December 2016 as Day 19 of Advent 2016. Timeline retains 012-013.M31 but as a derived value: Lexicanum's Typhus article places the Zaramund asylum immediately before Typhon rejoins Mortarion at the purging of Ynyx, and dates the Fall of the Death Guard to 013-014.M31, so this sits just before that. Note Zaramund is also where Typhon was first converted to Chaos during the Great Crusade, which the title plays on.

entries.title: THE PAINTED COUNT
entries.notes: Worst faction error in the batch is fixed: there are no Blood Angels here. 'The Painted Count' is Gendor Skraivok's own epithet, earned for his Nostraman noble ancestry and his war paint, and the story is Night Lords aboard the Nightfall, following directly from Guy Haley's novel Pharos and the short story A Safe and Shadowed Place. The manifest's Blood Angels tag would have shown a traitor story under a loyalist filter. Published 13 December 2016 as Day 13 of Advent 2016. Dated 009.M31 from Lexicanum's date for the Battle of Sotha, which this immediately follows. Note the Track of Words review calls him 'Garreth' Skraivok; Lexicanum and the Black Library copy both give Gendor, which is used here.

entries.title: THE LAST SON OF PROSPERO
entries.notes: Not a redemption-in-battle story: it is set on Terra in Malcador's custody and is the origin of Janus, first Supreme Grand Master of the Grey Knights. White Scars added, as the Khan is central and Arvida's whole arc comes out of Scars and The Path of Heaven. Published 24 December 2016 as Day 24 of Advent 2016. Timeline retains 012-013.M31 but as a derived value rather than the blanket: it follows the White Scars' arrival on Terra at the end of The Path of Heaven and precedes the Siege.

entries.title: THE SOUL, SEVERED
entries.notes: Manifest had this as 'Various' with a vague warp-and-souls blurb; it is a specific Emperor's Children succession story and the source of Eidolon's title 'the Soul-Severed'. Format confirmed Audio Drama, Day 9 of Advent 2016, 25 minutes. Setting identified as the chem-world Horvia from Lexicanum's Eidolon article, which cites this story for the Archorian confrontation. Timeline 012.M31 is derived by sequence: it falls after the Battle of Catallus and Eidolon's pursuit of the White Scars, and before Fulgrim recalls the Legion in Slaves to Darkness (013.M31).

entries.title: DARK COMPLIANCE
entries.notes: Format Audio Drama confirmed by Lexicanum (released July 2017, Ramon Tikaram as Horus, Jonathan Keeble as Argonis); Lexicanum notes it was later also printed as prose in this anthology, so if the site distinguishes original format from anthology format the Audio Drama tag is the right one. 'Various' replaced with Sons of Horus plus Mechanicum, Accazzar-Beta being a loyalist Mechanicum forge world. Timeline 012.M31 is derived, not quoted: Track of Words places it after Tallarn (Lexicanum: 010-012.M31) and before the final push on Terra.

entries.title: DUTY WAITS
entries.notes: Legion was already correct; blurb was generic and missed the actual event, which is a civilian riot rather than a battle. Published as Day 4 of the Advent 2017 subscription. Dated 013.M31: it sits after the Alpha Legion infiltration of Praetorian of Dorn and with four primarchs already mustered on Terra, and Lexicanum dates the Siege itself to 014.M31, so this is the year immediately before.

entries.title: MAGISTERIUM
entries.notes: Checked from scratch as instructed. Manifest's 'Custodians prepare to defend the Emperor' was close in flavour but wrong in substance: this is the aftermath of the Webway War, not preparation, and the drama is Valdor versus Dorn plus Prospero flashbacks. Viewpoint character is the Custodian Samonas, who Lexicanum also places at the Unification-era coup, Prospero and the webway. Imperial Fists added for Dorn. Published as Day 7 of the Advent 2017 subscription. Dated 013.M31: after The Master of Mankind and the close of the fighting in the webway, and before the Siege proper, which Lexicanum dates 119014-593014.M31.

entries.title: NOW PEALS MIDNIGHT
entries.notes: Manifest said the traitor fleet emerges and the Siege begins; both sources are clear that nothing actually happens, that there is no action at all, and that the story stops on the threshold. Corrected to reflect that. 'Various' narrowed to Imperial Fists, the confirmed focus being Dorn and his sons, though other loyalist forces on Terra feature. Published as part of the Advent 2017 calendar. Dated 013-014.M31 because Lexicanum has Horus's armada reach the Sol System on the first day of Primus, 014.M31, and this ends immediately before that.

entries.title: DREAMS OF UNITY
entries.notes: IMPORTANT, this partly contradicts the audit note I was given. The brief said the story is largely a Unification Wars flashback featuring Kabe and the siege of Abyssna, with an effective setting in mid-to-late M30. Both sources say otherwise. The present-day frame is the substance of the story: Heruk in The Maw and the Swathe beneath the Outer Palace, the burning of Tarrigata's ludus, and the Custodian Tagiomalchian hunting a possessed Alpha Legionary and eight cultists in the catacombs, explicitly after the Alpha Legion attack on Terra. Kabe is not a flashback character; he dies in a present-day pit fight in the opening scene. Abyssna, Ararat, Sibir and Albia appear as Heruk's hallucinations and memories. The protagonist is Dahren Heruk, not Kabe. Setting therefore dated 013.M31, Terra, immediately pre-Siege, with M30 Unification flashbacks noted here rather than in the timeline field. Published as Day 12 of the Advent 2017 subscription.

entries.title: THE BOARD IS SET
entries.notes: This was the closest of the sixteen to being right already, so the blurb needed refining rather than replacing. Corrected the detail that Malcador is the protagonist and the tone is contemplative and deliberately ambiguous, and that the Emperor is on the Golden Throne holding back what lies beneath the Palace rather than sitting across a table as an equal player. 'Various' replaced with Emperor and Custodian Guard; if the site prefers a single tag here, Emperor alone would be defensible. Published as Day 23 of the Advent 2017 calendar. Dated 013.M31 as the year before the Siege, per Lexicanum's dating of the Siege of Terra to 014.M31.

entries.title: SERPENT
entries.notes: The current data assigning this to the Alpha Legion appears to be a guess from the title. No Legiones Astartes force is identifiable in any source; the story is about the Davinite priesthood, so legions is set to the existing catalogue value 'Various' (the site vocabulary has no Chaos-cult faction). Format confirmed as prose short story: it was printed in the Weekender 2013 programme, and Black Library's audio release is an unabridged 12-minute audiobook reading rather than an audio drama. No source anchors the in-universe date, so 004.M31 is retained unverified.

entries.title: HUNTER'S MOON
entries.notes: Confirmed as flagged by the prior audit: Space Wolves versus Alpha Legion, not White Scars. Originally a 35-minute audio drama released on CD paired with Thief of Revelations, later collected in prose. Timeline moved from 004.M31 to 006.M31 because the plot turns on news of the Heresy having already broken; that is a reasoned anchor rather than a dated source, so treat the date as medium confidence.

entries.title: THIEF OF REVELATIONS
entries.notes: Legion was already correct. Format corrected to Audio Drama (approximately 35 minutes, released November 2013, full cast). Timeline moved from 004.M31 to 005.M31 because every source places the story after the fall of Prospero, which this site dates at 004-005.M31 (PROSPERO BURNS). The exact year is not stated in any source, so the date is medium confidence.

entries.title: VERITAS FERRUM
entries.notes: Legion and date were already correct. Format corrected: this was an audio drama released in the 2012 Black Library Advent Calendar, later adapted to prose for this anthology. The current blurb's framing around Iron Hands doctrine is generic; the actual story is a shipboard rescue dilemma at Isstvan V. No viewpoint character is named in any source I could reach, so mainCharacters is left empty rather than guessed.

entries.title: STRIKE AND FADE
entries.notes: Serious error corrected: this is Salamanders versus Night Lords, not Raven Guard. The prior data appears to have inferred 'guerrilla tactics' from the title and attached the wrong shattered Legion. Adding Night Lords also puts a traitor Legion on the record for this entry. Format corrected to Audio Drama (2012 Black Library Advent Calendar, roughly 10 minutes).

entries.title: BROTHERHOOD OF THE STORM
entries.notes: Confirmed as flagged: White Scars and Jaghatai Khan, and confirmed as the anthology's only novella. Type, legions and timeline were already right. The blurb is rewritten because the current one describes an allegiance crisis, whereas the novella is actually the Chondax ork campaign with Shiban Khan as the main viewpoint. Orks feature heavily but there is no Ork entry in the site's faction vocabulary, so they are described in the blurb instead. The 007.M31 date is retained; Chondax runs immediately into Scars, which the site also dates 007.M31.

entries.title: HONOUR TO THE DEAD
entries.notes: Substantially wrong before: this is a Titan Legions story, not an Ultramarines revenge tale. Legio Praesagius (True Messengers, loyalist) against the Fire Masters (traitor) over Ithraca on Calth, with a civilian family as the human viewpoint. Ultramarines are present only as scattered offscreen forces. Collegia Titanica added as the primary faction. Format corrected to Audio Drama (roughly 74 minutes, full cast, first released 2013). No named viewpoint character is confirmed by a source, so mainCharacters is left empty.

entries.title: BUTCHER'S NAILS
entries.notes: The existing blurb was broadly right about the Angron and Lorgar relationship. Corrected: format is Audio Drama (August 2012), and Word Bearers added alongside World Eaters since Lorgar and his Legion are half the story. Timeline left at 007-008.M31; the story sits just ahead of Betrayer, which this site dates 007.M31, so the existing range already covers it.

entries.title: KRYPTOS
entries.notes: Confirmed as flagged: Raven Guard and Iron Hands at Cavor Sarta, nothing to do with Mars or the Mechanicum civil war. The prior entry listed Mechanicum alone and set the story on Mars, which stripped both loyalist Legions off the record. Mechanicum is retained because the antagonists are the Dark Mechanicum of Cavor Sarta. Format (Short Story, June 2012 eBook) and date were already correct. Protagonist names cross-checked against a Goodreads plot summary and Graham McNeill's own site.

entries.title: WOLF'S CLAW
entries.notes: The current blurb was pure title-guessing. This is a specific Bjorn origin piece: how he gained his claw at Alaxxes. Alpha Legion added as the antagonist Legion. Format corrected to Audio Drama (March 2014, roughly 10 minutes) - Black Library's own page labels it 'A Horus Heresy audio drama', in contrast to Lone Wolf which it labels an unabridged audiobook.

entries.title: WARMASTER
entries.notes: Legion and date left as they were. Format corrected to Audio Drama (December 2012, roughly 9 minutes). Sources confirm there is a twist about who Horus is speaking to but none of them state who it is, so the blurb notes the twist exists without inventing the answer. No source anchors the in-universe year, so 008.M31 is retained unverified.

entries.title: THE DIVINE WORD
entries.notes: Serious error corrected: this has nothing to do with the Word Bearers. It is a loyalist story about Marcus Valerius of the Therion Cohort serving with the Raven Guard, and the origins of Emperor-worship. Leaving it tagged Word Bearers would place a loyalist story on the traitor side of any faction filter. Format kept as Short Story (22 pages, July 2013); the Black Library MP3 is an unabridged reading of the prose, not an audio drama. Date left unchanged as no source anchors it.

entries.title: KHÂRN: THE EIGHTFOLD PATH
entries.notes: Confirmed as flagged: World Eaters. Legion and date unchanged. Format corrected to Audio Drama (released 8 December 2013, roughly 13 minutes, full cast). The blurb is replaced because the current one is an abstract restatement rather than the actual fighting-pit setting.

entries.title: CYPHER: GUARDIAN OF ORDER
entries.notes: Legion was already right. Format corrected to Audio Drama (roughly 9 minutes, full cast). The current blurb implied a Heresy-front warrior story; it is actually a Caliban home-world piece with Zahariel as the viewpoint. Date retained at 008.M31 but flagged: the Zahariel and Luther Northwilds arc spans roughly 006-009.M31 across Fallen Angels and Angels of Caliban, and no source pins this story to a year.

entries.title: HEART OF THE CONQUEROR
entries.notes: The current blurb was a generic 'descent into madness' restatement. The story is actually a mortal Navigator's first-person reflection, with Lorgar appearing. Format stays Short Story (Weekender 2014 programme, later a quick read), which is worth noting because most other Legacies entries of this length are audio dramas. Word Bearers added for Lorgar. Date left unchanged; sources place it after Betrayer (007.M31 on this site) without giving a year.

entries.title: LUCIUS: THE ETERNAL BLADEMASTER
entries.notes: Confirmed as flagged: Emperor's Children. Thousand Sons added because Sanakht is the co-lead. Format corrected to Audio Drama (released 21 December 2013). Note that Black Library also lists this story as 'Lucius: The Eternal Blade'; the manifest title is retained. Date left unchanged; sources place it after Iydris (Angel Exterminatus, 007.M31 on this site) without giving a year.

entries.title: CENSURE
entries.notes: Serious error corrected: this is Ultramarines versus Word Bearers on Calth, not a Salamanders story. The prior entry appears to have attached Nick Kyme's usual Legion by default. Format corrected to Audio Drama (roughly 75 minutes, full cast). Date retained at 009.M31, which is consistent with the Underworld War having 'raged for years' after Calth (007.M31 on this site).

entries.title: BJORN: LONE WOLF
entries.notes: Legion, date and Short Story type all stand. Type deliberately not changed to Audio Drama: Goodreads records it as a nine-page prose piece from the Black Library Advent Calendar 2013, and Black Library's own audio page calls it 'A Horus Heresy unabridged audiobook' with a single narrator, unlike the sibling Wolf's Claw which it explicitly calls an audio drama. Blurb replaced because the current one is a title paraphrase with no actual content. Date is unverified; no source gives a year for Velbayne.

entries.title: RIVEN
entries.notes: Legions changed from the placeholder 'Various' to Iron Hands, which is what the story is about. Imperial Fists deliberately not added: Rogal Dorn issues the mission but the Legion itself is not a participant. Format (Short Story) is correct. Date flagged as doubtful rather than changed: the plot is triggered by news of Ferrus Manus's death at Isstvan V (006.M31 on this site), which sits awkwardly with the current 011.M31, but no source gives an in-universe year and 011.M31 may reflect a deliberate placement alongside the Shattered Legions material, so it is left alone.

entries.title: DESCENT OF ANGELS
entries.notes: Content of the old blurb was broadly right but it omitted the actual viewpoint character, Zahariel El'Zurias, and read as though the Lion were the protagonist. Both the Fandom and Wikipedia synopses make Zahariel the narrator, with the first half on pre-Imperial Caliban and the second half following the early Great Crusade. Timeline end corrected from 970.M30: the Lion is found on Caliban in 846.M30 (Lion El'Jonson page), and Fallen Angels, which picks up directly where this novel ends, opens in the 147th year of the Great Crusade, which the same page's dating makes roughly 945.M30 (it dates the 200th year as 998.M30). Wikipedia independently says the novel concludes about 50 years before the Heresy. The 820.M30 start is carried over unverified, hence medium confidence.

entries.title: THE FIRST HERETIC
entries.notes: Blurb and blurbSafe verified and carried through unchanged. Every element checks out: the censure for the Word Bearers' worship of the Emperor on Khur, the Pilgrimage of Lorgar (which the Fandom Pilgrimage page confirms passes through the Cadia System before entering the Eye of Terror), the Legion's fall to Chaos, and Erebus engineering the Warmaster's corruption. Timeline moved from 956.M30 to 959.M30: the Fandom novel page states the book starts 47 years before Isstvan V, dated ca. 006.M31, giving 959.M30; Wikipedia says 43 years before Isstvan V and the Pilgrimage page says 43 years before the Heresy, giving 962-963.M30. No source supports 956.M30. Note the novel spans roughly 50 years and ends with the Word Bearers en route to Calth (007.M31), a span the single-millennium date format cannot express, so the opening year is used.

entries.title: LEGION
entries.notes: Blurb accurate, carried through unchanged. The Cabal's proposition is exactly as described: the Alpha Legion page sets out the two futures, one in which the Emperor wins and humanity is slowly consumed by Chaos over ten to twenty millennia, and one in which Horus wins, humanity is destroyed, and the Chaos Gods starve. Setting is the compliance of Nurth, protagonists Alpharius and Omegon plus Imperial Army officers of the Geno Five-Two Chiliad and the Cabal agent John Grammaticus. Timeline left at 001.M31 but flagged: sources conflict. Wikipedia and the Alpha Legion page both say the story runs about two years before the Heresy begins, while the Alpha Legion campaign list dates the Nurth compliance to ca. 999.M30. 001.M31 sits between them and nothing directly contradicts it.

entries.title: A THOUSAND SONS
entries.notes: Verified against the Fandom plot summary and Wikipedia and carried through unchanged: censure at the Council of Nikaea, continued secret sorcery on Prospero, Magnus foreseeing Horus's fall, the psychic warning breaching the Emperor's webway project beneath the Imperial Palace, the Emperor dispatching Leman Russ, and the flesh-change and Tzeentch's hand in the Legion's fate. The Council of Nikaea is dated 001.M31 on the Fandom wiki, supporting the start of the given range.

entries.title: HORUS RISING
entries.notes: Reported error confirmed and fixed. The old blurb and blurbSafe both claimed Horus is wounded by the anathame on Davin's moon in this book. That happens in False Gods (book II). The Fandom Anathame page states the blade was stolen by Erebus from the Interex's Hall of Devices in Xenobia Principis and was then used, through events orchestrated by Erebus, to mortally injure Horus on the plague moon of Davin. The Interex page confirms the theft and the resulting war are the Xenobia debacle, and the official False Gods synopsis on the series list page opens with the Warmaster putting the debacle with the Interex behind him. The rewritten blurb now ends where the novel ends. blurbSafe reveals nothing about Erebus, the theft or any wounding, which matters because a new reader starts here. Timeline left at 002-003.M31 and flagged: Wikipedia places the novel in the 203rd year of the Great Crusade, which the Lion El'Jonson page's dating would make roughly 001.M31, but no source gives an explicit M31 date for the book so the existing value is retained.

entries.title: FALSE GODS
entries.notes: Everything the old blurb said was accurate, but it opened with Horus already dying, which left the wounding on Davin's moon attached to no book at all and let the Horus Rising error stand unchallenged. Both texts now place the anathame wound where it belongs, in this novel. Detail is from the Fandom False Gods plot summary: Erebus reports Davin non-compliant, the Sons of Horus land on the swamp moon, Horus goes on alone to Temba's grounded flagship, Temba is mutated by his worship of Nurgle and wields the Kinebrach anathame, and Erebus persuades the Mournival to take Horus to the Temple of the Serpent Lodge, where the induced vision of the Emperor's apotheosis turns him. blurbSafe stops short of saying Horus falls.

entries.title: THE OUTCAST DEAD
entries.notes: Broadly accurate and carried through unchanged. Confirmed: the first novel-length story in the series set almost entirely on Terra, Kai Zulane a former Ultramarines-attached astropath who unwittingly becomes keeper of a secret about how the Heresy ends, a mixed band of Space Marines suspected of treachery held beneath the Imperial Palace, and a manhunt through Terra's underworld involving the Emperor's Custodians. Two small looseness points not worth a rewrite: Zulane absorbs the secret from another mind rather than receiving a prophetic vision of his own, and the novel's chronological anchor is Magnus's psychic assault on the Imperial Palace rather than a galaxy-wide eruption. Wikipedia dates the action from several months before that event to several months after, supporting the 004.M31 timeline.

entries.title: PROSPERO BURNS
entries.notes: Real error found and fixed. The old blurb said Magnus 'breaks his own spine teleporting the survivors into the warp'. The Fandom Magnus the Red page describes the duel plainly: Magnus punctures one of Russ's hearts, Russ kicks him in his single eye and then lifts Magnus into the air and breaks his back over his knee. It was Russ who broke Magnus's spine, and it was Tzeentch, not Magnus, who then transported Tizca into the Eye of Terror in exchange for Magnus's eternal fealty. The rest of the old blurb was correct, including Horus twisting the Emperor's order of apprehension into an order of destruction, which the same page confirms. blurbSafe was rewritten because the old one revealed Horus's interference, which is a betrayal reveal.

entries.title: GALAXY IN FLAMES
entries.notes: Error found and fixed. Both old texts put Nathaniel Garro on the ground surviving the virus bombardment alongside Loken and Tarvitz. The Fandom Eisenstein page says the opposite: Garro lost most of his right leg in an earlier action in the Isstvan system, and the time needed to adjust to the augmetic meant he could not be declared fit for combat duty on Isstvan III, where he would otherwise have been among the loyalists caught in the virus-bombing. He was in orbit, where he seized the Eisenstein. Also softened 'a second bombardment that reduces the planet to atomic fire': the Isstvan III Atrocity page describes a final conventional high-explosive bombardment that flattened the Choral City, not an atomic one. Tarvitz's warning and Loken's resistance in the ruins are confirmed by the same page.

entries.title: MECHANICUM
entries.notes: Corrected an unsupported framing and a significant omission. Both old texts opened with 'As Terra reels from Magnus's psychic assault, Mars erupts into civil war'. Neither the Fandom Mechanicum page nor the Schism of Mars page mentions Magnus anywhere in connection with the Martian civil war, and the novel predates A Thousand Sons in publication; the war is driven by Horus's agents and Kelbor-Hal's grievance over withheld knowledge. Replaced with the sourced framing. Also added the Dalia Cythera and Dragon of Mars thread, which is roughly half the novel and was missing entirely. Kelbor-Hal's bargain for the knowledge sealed by the Treaty of Mars, the persecution of loyalist tech-priests and the Titan war are all confirmed. Timeline left at 005.M31, noting the Schism of Mars page dates the wider civil war 005-006.M31.

entries.title: THE FLIGHT OF THE EISENSTEIN
entries.notes: Corrected an over-claim. The old blurb closed by saying Garro's journey marks him as the first of Malcador's Knights-Errant, 'the warriors who will become the founding members of the Grey Knights'. The Knights-Errant page dates that body's founding to 005.M31 and shows the Grey Knights were founded in 014.M31 from just eight psychic Knights-Errant chosen as the 'Titans'; Garro, though Agentia Primus, was not among them, and his recruitment by Malcador belongs to the later Garro stories rather than to this novel. Removed. Everything else verified: the Seventy, the flight from Isstvan III, the life-eater outbreak aboard involving Grulgor, the Eisenstein left crippled in the warp and found by Rogal Dorn's fleet (Fandom Eisenstein page), and the disbelief Garro meets from Imperial authorities (Wikipedia).

entries.title: FALLEN ANGELS
entries.notes: Corrected a major omission and a misleading closing line. The old blurb covered only the Caliban half and closed with 'When the Lion returns, he will find his homeworld has become a fortress of rebellion', which invites the reader to expect the Lion's return in this book. He does not return to Caliban here. The Fandom plot summary and Wikipedia both describe two parallel threads, the second being the Lion's race to secure the forge world Diamat and its secret Titan-scale siege engines before Horus can, with Chaplain Nemiel leading the strike force into a Dark Mechanicum betrayal. Added that, plus the Caliban insurgency and the warp entity beneath the Northwilds arcology. Timeline left at 005.M31, the Diamat thread and the arrival of news of Horus's treachery, noting the Caliban thread reaches back to roughly 945.M30, a span the single-millennium format cannot carry.

entries.title: FEAR TO TREAD
entries.notes: Reported error confirmed and fixed. The old blurb closed with the Blood Angels being 'delayed from reaching Terra in time to prevent the Dropsite Massacre'. The Drop Site Massacre took place at Isstvan V, not Terra, and the Fandom page dates it to ca. 006.M31. The purpose of the Signus trap, per the Signus Campaign page, was to isolate and corrupt the IX Legion, and Wikipedia's synopsis states that while the Blood Angels were fighting at Signus, Horus's rebellion erupted openly and the loyalists suffered catastrophic losses in the Dropsite Massacre, after which Sanguinius turned for Terra. Rewritten accordingly. Also corrected the flaw: the Signus Campaign page names the Red Thirst as the curse Horus set out to exploit, with the campaign producing the first reported instance of the Black Rage rather than the Black Rage driving the plot. Ka'Bandha and the daemonic host are confirmed, as is the 005-006.M31 dating.

entries.title: FULGRIM
entries.notes: Real error fixed: the old blurb said 'the daemon and Primarch merge, creating a being of terrible beauty and horror'. The Fandom Fulgrim article is explicit that the Greater Daemon is freed from the sword and fully possesses Fulgrim's body, trapping the primarch's consciousness in the portrait hanging in La Fenice aboard the Pride of the Emperor. There is no merger; Fulgrim only reverses the swap later, in The Reflection Crack'd. Date re-anchored from 006.M31 to 005-006.M31 per Lexicanum's chronology page. Note the sources disagree on the start: Lexicanum's footnote says its 005-006 dating is drawn from Parts 4 and 5 only, while Tymell dates the opening Laeran campaign to mid-002.M31. 005-006.M31 covers the Heresy-era bulk without dragging the book four years earlier in a sorted list. blurbSafe verified accurate and left unchanged.

entries.title: VULKAN LIVES
entries.notes: Blurb verified and carried through unchanged. Vulkan is held on a Night Lords gaol-hulk, killed repeatedly, and finally escapes the Iron Labyrinth (built for Curze by Perturabo) using the teleporter in Dawnbringer. Only correction needed is the faction list: the entire second strand of the novel follows Artellus Numeon's Isstvan survivors on Traoris against the Word Bearers under Dark Apostle Valdrekk Elias and the huntsman Barthusa Narek, with Erebus appearing in person, so Word Bearers is added. Date 006-007.M31 confirmed: Tymell splits the book into 'late 30,006 and late 30,007', and the Horus Heresy Journal dates Vulkan's capture to 568.006.M31.

entries.title: DELIVERANCE LOST
entries.notes: Two real errors fixed. First, 'Corax is forced to mercy-kill his own sons' is wrong: the Fandom Corax article states he declared the mutants were still Raven Guard and vowed to reverse their condition, and the mutants then saved the Legion's original gene-seed at Ravendelve, after which Corax let those able to fight join the Raptor squads. Second, 'the results are horrific, mutated abominations instead of Astartes' understates the sequence: the first 500 Raptors were a success, and only the second cadre of 2,000 mutated after the sabotage. Also removed the forward reference to Corax's later disappearance into the Eye of Terror, which is outside this novel. Timeline kept at 007.M31: Tymell spans the book November 006 to early 008, but the rescue is the prologue and the overwhelming bulk of the narrative present (Terra, the Deliverance rebuild, the Alpha Legion sabotage) falls in 007.

entries.title: THE CRIMSON KING
entries.notes: Biggest date error in the batch: 007.M31 was three years too early. Tymell dates the novel to 30,010, notes Lorgar refers to Horus as reborn (so after Vengeful Spirit), and cites Horus Heresy Book VIII (Malevolence) confirming Ahriman's attack on Kamiti Sona takes place in 010. Re-anchored to 010.M31. Blurb also corrected: the old text framed the book as Legion politics inside Tzeentch's realm, but the story is a galaxy-spanning shard-hunt (Kamiti Sona, Nikaea, Prospero) pursued by warriors Malcador deploys, per Track of Words. Dropped the invented 'choose whether to serve Horus or chart his own dark path' and replaced it with the sourced ending: Magnus is restored except for one shard remaining on Terra.

entries.title: THE DAMNATION OF PYTHOS
entries.notes: Date corrected from 007.M31 to 006.M31: Tymell dates the novel to August 30,006, and its internal references place it a few weeks after Isstvan V, directly following the audio drama Veritas Ferrum. Confidence is medium on the date only because no source gives an end point for the Pythos garrison's stay. Blurb correction: 'Pythos becomes a daemon world' is not supportable. The Fandom Pythos article describes the subterranean warp portal, the Damnation Cache, as dating from the Horus Heresy but remaining sealed until Abaddon reopened it in 959-961.M41, so the world was not left as a permanent daemon world. Reworded to the buried gateway and the doom of the sanctuary. Protagonist and legion mix confirmed by Track of Words: Captain Durun Atticus and the 111th company of Iron Hands plus smaller Raven Guard and Salamanders contingents. Only Atticus is listed under mainCharacters because he is the only name I could confirm from a source in this pass.

entries.title: NEMESIS
entries.notes: Malcador's role is confirmed, not an error: the Fandom Execution Force article names him the secret Grand Master of Assassins who authorised the first Execution Force. The real error was Spear. He is not 'Horus's own weapon' deployed against the Execution Force; he is an escaped Culexus experiment captured and daemon-bonded by Erebus of the Word Bearers, and Erebus tasked him with killing the Emperor. Word Bearers added to the faction list accordingly. Also added the outcome, which the old blurb left hanging: the Dagonet attempt failed and all but one of the assassins were killed. Date widened from 007.M31 to 007-008.M31: Tymell puts the opening at mid-to-late 007 and cites Forge World Horus Heresy Book VI giving the Dagonet assassination as year 008; the Fandom article likewise places the novel about two standard years after Isstvan V.

entries.title: KNOW NO FEAR
entries.notes: Everything checks out. Lexicanum's chronology page and its Battle of Calth article both give 007.M31, and Tymell dates the novel to July 30,007. The Lorgar humiliation at Monarchia is dated roughly forty years before the Heresy, so 'decades of resentment' is right. Guilliman being blown into vacuum is accurate: Lorgar's incantation summons daemons that smash into the bridge of the Macragge's Honour and vent it to space. The aftermath is accurate too: the Veridian sun was irreversibly poisoned, Calth's atmosphere permanently stripped, and the population driven into the cavern cities. Carried through unchanged.

entries.title: BATTLE FOR THE ABYSS
entries.notes: Date confirmed at 007.M31 by Lexicanum's chronology page; Tymell notes the climax is simultaneous with Kor Phaeron's attack on Calth. Blurb corrected at the end: 'The mission succeeds, but barely, and Macragge is warned' is not what happens. Per the Fandom Furious Abyss article the ship is destroyed en route, before it can put its plan against Macragge into motion, when Cestus, Brynngar and Skraal sabotage the plasma generatorium; Cestus kills Fleet-Captain Zadkiel and dies aboard. Also tightened the target description: the plan was to destroy the moon Formaska and then virus-bomb Macragge behind the debris, not a direct assault. Thousand Sons retained in the faction list from the manifest on the strength of the loyalist band's Thousand Sons member, though the Fandom article names only Ultramarines, Space Wolves and World Eaters.

entries.title: ANGEL EXTERMINATUS
entries.notes: Second big date error: 007.M31 was two years too early. Tymell dates the novel early to mid-30,009 and states the Horus Heresy Journal confirms it begins in early 009 and ends in mid-009; his summary official timeline also gives 'Early 009.M31, Perturabo and Fulgrim join forces to pursue the Angel Exterminatus' and 'Mid-009.M31, Fulgrim ascends to daemonhood'. Re-anchored to 009.M31. Blurb verified accurate in every particular and left unchanged, including the sacrifice: the maugetar stone Fulgrim gifts Perturabo drains his life to fuel the apotheosis, and there is no xenos weapon at all, since Fulgrim intends to become the Angel Exterminatus himself. Legions extended: the Black Library synopsis has the traitors 'pursued by vengeful survivors from Isstvan V', and those are the Shattered Legions crew of the Sisypheum, the Iron Hand Sabak Wayland and the Raven Guard Nykona Sharrowkyn among them.

entries.title: BETRAYER
entries.notes: Accurate as written. Tymell dates the book July to late 30,007 and his official timeline gives 'Shadow Crusade begins, and Angron ascends to daemon princehood' in 007.M31. The Fandom Angron article confirms the Butcher's Nails were killing him at an accelerating rate after Calth, that Lorgar took him back to Nuceria on the pretext of studying the implants, and that Lorgar intended to force his ascension regardless. Khârn's presence and Guilliman's pursuit are both correct. The only thing the blurb leaves out is that the ascension takes place on Nuceria, Angron's homeworld, and that Guilliman confronts them there in person, but nothing stated is wrong, so it is carried through unchanged.

entries.title: SCARS
entries.notes: Date confirmed at 007.M31: Tymell dates the novel to February 30,007 and his official timeline places the Alaxxes contact at 108.007.M31. Blurb corrected on the decisive point. The old text said the Khan is swayed 'when he learns the truth about the Word Bearers' manipulation'. The Word Bearers are not in this book. It is the Alpha Legion that blockades Chondax and manipulates the White Scars, per both the Black Library synopsis and the Fandom Jaghatai Khan article, and the Khan's mind is settled at ruined Prospero and in his confrontation with Mortarion, who arrives of his own accord to recruit him and duels him among the ruins of Tizca. Legion list extended to Alpha Legion, Death Guard and Space Wolves, all of whom feature substantially. The internal purge is real: the lodge coup is led by Hasik Noyan-Khan and opposed by Shiban Khan.

entries.title: VENGEFUL SPIRIT
entries.notes: Date tightened from 008-009.M31 to 009.M31. Lexicanum's Battle of Molech infobox gives 009.M31, Tymell dates the novel October to November 30,009, and his official timeline entry is 906.009.M31 for Horus leading the attack on Molech. One Forge World-derived list does place Molech in year 008, which is presumably where the 008 start came from, but three sources agree on 009 and the 008 start pulls the book too early. Blurb corrected on one factual point: the Emperor's visit to Molech was not 'millennia ago'. Molech was brought to compliance in 869.M30, roughly 140 years before the battle, with Horus, Fulgrim, the Lion and Jaghatai present. Also added House Devine's betrayal, which decides the campaign. Death Guard added to the faction list: Mortarion and the bulk of the XIV Legion fight the whole campaign alongside the Sons of Horus.

entries.title: THE UNREMEMBERED EMPIRE
entries.notes: The back half of the old blurb described events from later books, not this one. Nobody learns that Terra still stands in The Unremembered Empire, the Imperium Secundus is not wound up here (that happens in Ruinstorm, late 011.M31), and there is no race for Terra. What actually happens, per the Fandom Vulkan and Imperium Secundus articles: Vulkan arrives on Macragge after teleporting away from Curze, his mind broken by the fall; Curze reaches Macragge too and comes close to assassinating Guilliman before being defeated; John Grammaticus kills Vulkan with the fulgurite spear on the Cabal's orders; and Sanguinius arrives at the very end to be crowned. Date widened from 009.M31 to 009-010.M31: Tymell dates the book November 30,009 to early 30,010 and notes the Forge World timeline puts Sanguinius's arrival, at the very end, in 010. Legions extended to include the Night Lords (Curze) and Salamanders (Vulkan and the surviving XVIII Legion).

entries.title: PHAROS
entries.notes: Real error corrected: the Night Lords do not attack to destroy the beacon and blind the loyalists, they attack to capture it and use it to find the Nightfall and reunite the Legion after their defeat in the Thramas Crusade. Barabas Dantioch, a loyalist Iron Warrior, is the device's keeper and the man who overloads it at the cost of his life, so Iron Warriors added to the faction list. Battle of Sotha is dated ~009.M31, so the existing timeline is confirmed. The Tyranid coda in the existing blurb is correct and has been kept.

entries.title: DEATHFIRE
entries.notes: Real error corrected: the existing blurb calls it a quest 'to find Vulkan', but Vulkan's body is never lost. It is already in a stasis casket on Macragge and the book is about smuggling it home to Nocturne. Word Bearers (Quor Gallek, Barthusa Narek), Death Guard and Ultramarines added as featured factions from the dramatis personae. Numeon's death as the final sacrifice, and Vulkan's rebirth from the Unbound Flame, are confirmed on the Vulkan article. Timeline left at 010.M31: no source consulted gives a specific date for this novel, so it has not been changed.

entries.title: TALLARN
entries.notes: Three real errors. (1) Scale: the existing blurb says 'billions of Imperial Guard tankers'. Sources give roughly ten million armoured vehicles committed and over a million wrecks left behind, and the M31 term is Imperial Army, not Imperial Guard (the Tallarn Desert Raiders regiments are only raised about twenty years later). (2) Timeline: both wikis date the Battle of Tallarn to 010-011.M31, not 010-012.M31. Range start is unchanged, so this does not move the sort position. (3) The 'ancient buried secret' is nameable: the Cursus of Alganar, also called the Black Oculus, a blackstone warp gateway. Format flagged: this is book 45 of the series but is formally a collected volume of one novel (Ironclad), one novella (Executioner) and two short stories (Siren, Witness), so type is set to Anthology rather than Novel. Change that back to Novel if the site groups it with the standalone novels. Alpha Legion, Iron Hands and Sons of Horus added as featured factions.

entries.title: PRAETORIAN OF DORN
entries.notes: The existing blurb was substantially accurate and its central spoiler (Dorn kills Alpharius) is correct. One soft error fixed: it credits Rogal Dorn with running the counter-infiltration, when the protagonist and title character is Archamus, master of the Huscarls, who conducts the hunt with Sergeant Kestros and the Selenar psyker Andromeda-17 and dies at Pluto. The mechanics of the duel are also specific: Alpharius impales Archamus with the Pale Spear, Dorn takes a killing stroke on purpose to trap Alpharius and kills him with the chainsword Storm's Teeth. Existing blurb was also five sentences, over the length guide. Timeline left at 010.M31, no source consulted contradicts it.

entries.title: THE MASTER OF MANKIND
entries.notes: No factual errors found in the existing text, so it is carried through almost verbatim. Two light touches only: the two em dashes were replaced with commas for house style, and the Mechanicum of Fabricator-General Zagreus Kane was named, since the official Black Library synopsis lists it as the third loyalist force alongside the Custodians and Sisters of Silence. Mechanicum and Thousand Sons (Magnus appears in person and is banished) added to the faction list. Timeline left at 011.M31: the War Within the Webway as a whole spans 004-014.M31, and no source pins this novel to a single year. For reference, the outcome is an Imperial defeat: Calastar falls, the Emperor abandons the Webway Project and seals the portal, and binds the daemon Drach'nyen into Tribune Ra Endymion. That is deliberately not in the blurb, which stops where the existing text stopped.

entries.title: THE PATH OF HEAVEN
entries.notes: Two real errors. (1) 'the Death Guard, now fully transformed by Nurgle's plague' is wrong for this point in the timeline. The Death Guard are not plague-ridden until the Destroyer Hive takes them in THE BURIED DAGGER, book 54, at 013.M31. (2) The Emperor's Children are co-equal antagonists with the Death Guard, named in the official Black Library synopsis and heavily represented in the dramatis personae through Eidolon, so they have been added to the faction list. Also reframed: the White Scars are not harrying the Death Guard to buy Terra time, they are being ground down and are searching for a route home. The climax is the Dark Glass webway station at the Battle of Catallus, where Yesugei sacrifices himself to open the portal. Sagyar Mazan detail in the existing text is correct and has been kept in the spoiler-free version.

entries.title: ANGELS OF CALIBAN
entries.notes: Real errors. The existing blurb says the Lion 'pursues the Night Lords through the Ruinstorm'. He does not: he hunts Konrad Curze personally, inside Ultramar and Imperium Secundus, and the Legion-level Night Lords war (the Thramas Crusade) is already over. The existing blurb also ends on 'the devastating realization that the Dark Angels' homeworld has turned traitor, and half the Legion has fallen with it', which overstates what happens here. Caliban's open fall comes later. In this book Luther and Zahariel consolidate control, Zahariel kills Lord Cypher and takes the title, and the Lion merely resolves to return home. Guilliman and Sanguinius are major on-page characters and have been added as factions. Lexicanum dates the main narrative 'At Ultramar in the year 11.M31', confirming the existing timeline.

entries.title: OLD EARTH
entries.notes: Two real errors. (1) 'Reunited with his Legion, Vulkan prepares for the final defense of Terra' is wrong. Vulkan travels with just three legionaries, the Draaksward (Abidemi, Zytos and Gargo), refuses to join the Shattered Legions' war, and reaches Terra with only them. (2) 'He brings with him a weapon designed for use against the Traitor forces' inverts the point. The Talisman of Seven Hammers is a doomsday device, a dead man's switch the Emperor intends Vulkan to trigger to consume Terra if Horus wins. Vulkan installs it in the Golden Throne and takes station at the Eternity Gate. Iron Hands, Raven Guard, Word Bearers and Imperial Fists added as featured factions from the dramatis personae. Timeline left at 011.M31, unverified but uncontradicted.

entries.title: RUINSTORM
entries.notes: Real error corrected. The existing blurb says the storm is 'powered by daemonic engines at Davin and other key locations' and that the primarchs 'must split up, each taking a separate path to destroy these focal points'. Neither is right. They travel together the whole way, guided first by Tuchulcha and then by corrupted Navigators taken at Anuari, and the climax is a single location, Davin, where Sanguinius duels the daemon Madail. The destruction of Davin by cyclonic torpedoes is what weakens the Ruinstorm. They only separate at the very end, with Guilliman and the Lion drawing off Horus's blockade so the Blood Angels can run for Terra. Word Bearers added as a featured faction. Second Battle of Davin is dated ~011.M31, confirming the existing timeline.

entries.title: WOLFSBANE
entries.notes: Two real errors, one of them an invented name. (1) The weapon is the Spear of Russ, not 'Gungnir'. A full-text search of the Warhammer 40k Fandom wiki for 'Gungnir' returns nothing, and Lexicanum names the Spear of Russ throughout: it was awarded to Russ after the Wheel of Fire Campaign and holds a portion of the Emperor's power, illuminating the truth to whatever it pierces. It was not 'forged by the Emperor Himself to wound a Primarch empowered by Chaos'. (2) 'The Chaos Gods restore their champion' does not happen here, it happens in SLAVES TO DARKNESS. What the spear actually does is strip the Molech-derived power out of Horus, which is why he is left near death in book 51. The confrontation is aboard the Vengeful Spirit over Trisolian A4, dated 012.M31, confirming the existing timeline. Belisarius Cawl gets his Heresy debut here, confirmed by Guy Haley in the Track of Words interview and by Lexicanum's dramatis personae. Mechanicum added as a faction.

entries.title: TITANDEATH
entries.notes: Corrections. (1) Outcome: the existing text says the loyalists 'eventually retreat' having bloodied the traitors. The recorded outcome of Beta-Garmon is a traitor victory, and Mohana Mankata VI, Great Mother of the Legio Solaria, is listed as killed in action. (2) Timeline extended to 012-013.M31. Lexicanum dates the second phase of Beta-Garmon, which is what this novel covers, to 012-013.M31, and puts the arrival of Sanguinius and Jaghatai Khan (both in the novel's dramatis personae) at 084013.M31. The range start is still 012, so the sort position does not move. Confidence is medium on the timeline only, because the novel is not itself dated. (3) Factions: the existing list of Collegia Titanica alone is too narrow. Fasadian Imperial Army infantry, Sanguinius with the Blood Angels, Jaghatai Khan with the White Scars, and Horus's own Sons of Horus armada all feature. Knights of House Procon Vi and Word Bearers attached to Legio Vulpa also appear but have been left off to keep the filter usable.

entries.title: SLAVES TO DARKNESS
entries.notes: Real error corrected. The existing blurb explains Horus's recovery as him purging the last of his humanity and the Chaos Gods restoring him: 'He purges the last remnants of his humanity, embracing full damnation... The Gods restore their champion, now more monster than man.' That is not what happens. Horus is wounded because the Spear of Russ stripped his Molech-derived power, and a fragment of his soul is holding out in the warp against enslavement. Maloghurst enters the immaterium by sorcery and gives his own life to convince that fragment to continue the rebellion and begin the Siege. Maloghurst is the character the Black Library synopsis itself foregrounds, and he was missing from the existing text entirely. Also added: Mortarion being sent ahead as vanguard, which is the direct hook into THE BURIED DAGGER. Faction list left as-is; the dramatis personae genuinely does cover all eight traitor Legions, so 'All Traitor Legions' is fair.

entries.title: THE BURIED DAGGER
entries.notes: The existing blurb was close but got the central horror backwards: 'Mortarion... watches his sons die in agony'. The point of the Destroyer Hive is that the Death Guard cannot die. They are made bloated and immortal and suffering, which is precisely why Mortarion has no way out. Also missing entirely was Calas Typhon, who engineers the whole thing by having the Navigators executed and steering the fleet himself, and who survives being killed twice. The Terra thread is more specific than 'Malcador continues forging the foundations': the Knights-Errant fight a Nurgle cult under the Lord of the Flies at White Mountain, Tylos Rubio is used as Erebus's unwitting assassin against Malcador, and the survivors are renamed the Nine Who Are Named and taken to Titan, becoming the forerunners of the Grey Knights. Loken and Garro are not among them. Knights-Errant added as a faction. Timeline left at 013.M31, uncontradicted.

entries.title: ROBOUTE GUILLIMAN: LORD OF ULTRAMAR
entries.notes: Old blurb was generic filler and never named the actual story. The book is the Battle of Thoas against orks, not a life-of-Guilliman overview, and Track of Words explicitly says it is not an origin story. The treatise excerpts are documentary epigraphs, not scenes, so they do not shift the narrative present. Timeline unchanged. Fandom's infobox calls this a Novella (240pp hardback) while Lexicanum and reviewers call it a novel; type set to Novel for consistency with the series, see batch note. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: LEMAN RUSS: THE GREAT WOLF
entries.notes: Old blurb named no plot at all. Structure confirmed twice: Track of Words says 'Wraight bookends the Dulan campaign with post-Heresy scenes', Tymell records the opening chapter as post-Heresy with the Space Wolves already a Chapter, and the closing section with news of the Lion's loss just reaching Fenris. Dark Angels added to legions because the Lion and his Legion are co-leads. Timeline left at the frame value 015-021.M31 per the existing dataset, though note the body of the book is the 870.M30 Dulan campaign, so the entry sorts a very long way from its content. Not a date change, just a flag. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: MAGNUS THE RED: MASTER OF PROSPERO
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described Magnus roaming the galaxy after forbidden knowledge and colliding with the Emperor's edicts, which is A Thousand Sons, not this book. This is a rescue mission on Morningstar shared with Perturabo. Iron Warriors added to legions: Perturabo and Forrix are co-leads. Frame confirmed by Tymell ('Opens sometime after the fall of Prospero, flashback to the evacuation of Morningstar in 29,853'). Timeline unchanged at 853.M30, which the book states twice; the frame remains undated in every source. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: PERTURABO: THE HAMMER OF OLYMPIA
entries.notes: Old blurb was roughly right about Olympia but omitted the hrud campaign entirely, which is half the book, and asserted 'his relationship with his adopted sister' as the novel's subject. Track of Words describes the split as Perturabo's early years versus the hrud campaign, with Dantioch and the legionary Fortreidon as the other viewpoints, so the sister claim is not sourced and has been dropped in favour of 'adoptive home world' and 'adoptive family', which are. Timeline unchanged at 999.M30; note the purge of Olympia at the end is dated 000.M31 by the novel and the Horus Heresy Journal but 004.M31 by Forge World, an existing known conflict. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: LORGAR: BEARER OF THE WORD
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it said the book examines Lorgar's crisis of faith after Monarchia and his discovery of the Chaos Gods. That is The First Heretic. Track of Words is explicit that the body is Colchis before the Emperor, 'barring a few post-Monarchia interludes', and that it is 'probably not the book for anyone wanting to see the Word Bearers in action'. Timeline unchanged at 959-964.M30, which is the frame value; the Colchis body runs roughly 841-857.M30. Kept the Monarchia interludes out of blurbSafe as they are a humiliation reveal. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: FULGRIM: THE PALATINE PHOENIX
entries.notes: Old blurb described the Legion's rebuilding from near-extinction and Fulgrim's fall to Slaanesh, neither of which is the plot; the rebuilding is background and the fall is Fulgrim (Book V). This is the III Legion's first solo compliance, on Byzas / Twenty-Eight One. Fabius appears as an early-stage apothecary, confirmed by Track of Words. Timeline unchanged at 850-868.M30, which remains inferred rather than stated: Tymell's estimate is '29,850s/860s?' and the in-book line about 'the intervening century since his rediscovery' contradicts the depicted state of the Legion. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: FERRUS MANUS: THE GORGON OF MEDUSA
entries.notes: SERIOUS ERROR REMOVED: the old blurb ended by saying his inflexibility 'leads to his death at Isstvan V'. The novel does not depict Isstvan V, and that is a major spoiler for a newcomer. The actual subject is the Fall of the Lords of Gardinaal. Emperor's Children added to legions: the III Legion contingent is a significant presence and a deliberate foil. Timeline unchanged at 869.M30, the best-evidenced date in this batch, cited by Lexicanum to the novel's own chapter 3 and to Horus Heresy Book Two. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: JAGHATAI KHAN: WARHAWK OF CHOGORIS
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described the Khan's early years on the steppes and his unification of Chogoris. The novel opens with him already found and meeting his Legion on Terra, and the Chogoris episode is one dated stop in the middle. Structure confirmed twice: Track of Words ('several short arcs spanning years of the Great Crusade') and Tymell's per-episode dates (Terra 879, Hoadh 881-884, Chogoris 898, Gar-Ban-Gar 906, Baal 908, Ullanor 000.M31). Timeline unchanged at 000.M31, the last episode. Note the Fandom page title misspells Chogoris as 'Chorgoris'. The book leads up to the Librarius debate but does not reach Nikaea. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: VULKAN: LORD OF DRAKES
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described Vulkan's discovery on Nocturne, his humanitarian philosophy and his Perpetual nature. None of that is the plot, and Vulkan has already been found and been away with the Emperor for years when the book opens. Annandale's own elevator pitch to Track of Words: 'This is the origin story of the Salamanders... currently two separate Legions, Nocturnean and Terran, who have never met.' Timeline unchanged at 845-855.M30, but flagging that this remains the weakest date in the batch: no source gives a year and the only firm bracket is post-835.M30, pre-Heresy. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: CORAX: LORD OF SHADOWS
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described the slave rebellion on Lycaeus before the Emperor found him. Track of Words is explicit that 'Corax's origin story has already been told' elsewhere and that this book instead examines justice versus vengeance during the Carinae compliance. Timeline unchanged at 954.M30, but note this is genuinely contested: the book's own '32 years since the Emperor came to Deliverance' is firm, while the rediscovery date it hangs off is not. Tymell prefers approximately 970s.M30, which would move this after Lorgar and Guilliman rather than before them. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: ANGRON: SLAVE OF NUCERIA
entries.notes: WORST ERROR IN THE BATCH. The old blurb said 'Angron returns to Nuceria during the Heresy' and that 'Lorgar offers him a terrible apotheosis'. Both are Betrayer, not this book. This is a Great Crusade novel set at Ghenna; Nuceria appears only as flashback and is not destroyed. Confirmed by Track of Words (Ghenna-era 'present' following Mago, 'past' showing Angron as a youth on Nuceria) and by Tymell ('Takes place at Ghenna, some time... after Angron is reunited with his legion'). Timeline unchanged at 900-905.M30. Note the book has an M41 coda following Kharn, which the dataset deliberately ignores for sorting. Fandom's page title pluralises the title as 'Slaves of Nuceria'; the correct title is the singular 'Slave of Nuceria', which the same page's infobox uses. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: KONRAD CURZE: THE NIGHT HAUNTER
entries.notes: Confirms the earlier finding: the frame is post-Heresy, not Heresy-era.
