Track of Words says Curze spends 'the final hours of his life' in a story 'long after the Heresy has ended', and Tymell independently places the present on Tsagualsa as Curze awaits his death, with the stasis pod recovered around 032.M31. Timeline unchanged at 036.M31. The Callidus assassin M'Shen is reported as present in the frame by secondary sources but I could not confirm her by name from a primary or first-hand source, so she is left out of mainCharacters and out of the blurb. blurbSafe deliberately omits the death frame, since the whole book is a spoiler for Curze's fate. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: LION EL'JONSON: LORD OF THE FIRST
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described the Lion's relationship with Luther and 'the betrayal festering on Caliban'. Neither Luther nor Caliban is the subject; that is Descent of Angels and Fallen Angels. This is the Northern Fringe Campaign against a xenos foe in the Muspel system. Guymer names the other viewpoints in his Track of Words interview: the Techmarine Duriel, the Librarian Aravain and the remembrancer Savine, and confirms the Ullanor Crusade is raging as the story opens. Timeline unchanged at 997.M30, the cleanest date in this batch. Do not move it to 000.M31 just because Ullanor is mentioned; Ullanor was multi-year and the Triumph is later. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: ALPHARIUS: HEAD OF THE HYDRA
entries.notes: Confirms the earlier finding: the book does NOT run into the Heresy. Tymell: 'Starts and ends with "Alpharius" (actually Omegon) being "found" by Horus late in the Crusade. Begins properly with Alpharius being discovered on Terra, right after the scattering of the Primarchs, before the Crusade has even begun.' Mike Brooks confirms to Track of Words that it is 'a first-person account of the Primarch of the Alpha Legion' and that he is 'of course the ultimate unreliable narrator'. Timeline unchanged at 981.M30. The old blurb was thematically defensible but described 'twin Primarchs' as the premise, which pre-empts a reveal, and gave no actual scope. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: MORTARION: THE PALE KING
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described Barbarus, the necromantic overlords and Mortarion's future servitude to Nurgle. The book is the Conquest of Galaspar; Barbarus appears only as motivation. Confirmed by the official Black Library synopsis on Lexicanum and by Lexicanum's Conquest of Galaspar article, which cites chapters 3, 4, 9 and 11 of this novel, and by Tymell ('Covers the conquest of Galaspar, the Death Guard's first after Mortarion takes command'). CAUTION on one point carried in tools/proposed-dates.json: it describes a frame set on Absyrtus about a year after Galaspar. I could not confirm that. Lexicanum's Absyrtus article sources the Absyrtus campaign entirely to a different story, The Verdict of the Scythe in Scions of the Emperor, and cites this novel nowhere. I have therefore kept Absyrtus out of the blurb. It does not affect the date either way. Timeline unchanged at 930-939.M30, which remains genuinely contested: Lexicanum's Galaspar infobox gives only 'M30'. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: ROGAL DORN: THE EMPEROR'S CRUSADER
entries.notes: SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb: it described Dorn as Praetorian fortifying the Imperial Palace, which is his Siege-era role, not this book. The body is the Night Crusade into the Occluda Noctis. Track of Words confirms 'Set quite early on in the Great Crusade... a campaign in which a full four Legions and their Primarchs were tasked with bringing the light of Compliance to the darkness of the Occluda Noctis... taking in not just Dorn but also Horus, Fulgrim and the Lion', told 'through the eyes of both his Legion and the Remembrancer Order', with Sigismund and Fafnir Rann among the viewpoints. Luna Wolves, Emperor's Children and Dark Angels added to legions on that basis. Timeline unchanged at 014.M31, the Terra frame, but flagging that roughly 208 pages are a Great Crusade campaign around 848-858.M30, so this entry currently sorts into the middle of the Siege sequence. Track of Words does not mention the Terra frame; it is attested by legiodraconis and by reviewer accounts recorded in tools/proposed-dates.json, hence medium confidence on that one element. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: SANGUINIUS: THE GREAT ANGEL
entries.notes: Confirms the earlier finding: this is late Great Crusade, and it never depicts Signus Prime or the Siege of Terra. SERIOUS CONTENT ERROR in the old blurb, which described visions of his own death, the gene-flaw and dying at Horus's hands. None of that is the book, and it spoils the character comprehensively for a newcomer. The official Black Library synopsis on Lexicanum confirms the discredited-remembrancer framing; Tymell confirms the muster at Baal 'fresh from Nikaea', the 'This. World. Is. Murder.' hand-off into Horus Rising, the six-month span across late 002 and early 003.M31, and the post-Heresy prologue and epilogue. Timeline unchanged at 002-003.M31. The remembrancer narrator is named as Avajis Kautenya in tools/proposed-dates.json but I could not confirm the name from an independent source, so it is omitted from mainCharacters. Confidence medium only because Track of Words never reviewed this one and Lexicanum carries the publisher blurb rather than a plot summary. Type set to Novella: the publisher calls all 17 short novels and both wikis call them novellas.

entries.title: ATHAME
entries.notes: Lexicanum carries a full scene-by-scene plot summary. The framing device is a narrator speaking to the dagger, confirmed independently by the Wordaholic Anonymous review ('a disjointed voice speaking to a blade'). The manifest date of 800.M30 is arbitrary: the story runs from pre-Imperial Terra through the early Great Crusade to Calth, and the site's NNN.MNN format cannot express that span, so it is anchored at its terminal point, the Battle of Calth in 007.M31 (Lexicanum, Battle of Calth). Legions changed from 'Various' to the two factions that actually carry the story, the Word Bearers (Anacreon, Arune Xen, Criol Fowst) and the Perpetuals (Oll Persson). The manifest blurb was not so much wrong as empty; it named no characters and no events.

entries.title: THE DARK KING
entries.notes: Confirmed: this is Curze and Nostramo. Format confirmed as a print short story, first published in the 2007 Games Day Horus Heresy Chapbook alongside The Lightning Tower and later collected in Shadows of Treachery; the Black Library audio release is a narration of the same short story, not an original audio drama, so 'Short Story' stands. Legions corrected: the Imperial Fists are central (Dorn, Sigismund, and the VII fleet that arrives over Nostramo), and Fulgrim's Phoenix Guard also feature. The manifest blurb was pure mood with no events; it never mentions Dorn, the assault or the destruction of Nostramo, which is the point of the story. Timeline of 984.M30 left unchanged: no source consulted gives a firm date for the destruction of Nostramo, and Lexicanum's Nostramo article carries none.

entries.title: DEATH OF A SILVERSMITH
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was invented from the title: it offers a general lament about war destroying art and gets the setting wrong. The story is a first-person deathbed monologue by an unnamed remembrancer silversmith aboard the Vengeful Spirit, murdered by an unnamed Luna Wolves captain who had commissioned a mould for wolf medallions. Legions changed from 'Various' to Luna Wolves and Remembrancers, both values already in use elsewhere on the site. Timeline moved from 000.M31 to 002.M31: the story is set after the Ullanor Triumph and the founding of the remembrancer order but while Hastur Sejanus is still alive, so immediately before the opening of Horus Rising, which the site dates 002-003.M31. Medium confidence applies to the date only.

entries.title: FEAT OF IRON
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was a generic character sketch of Ferrus Manus with no plot in it, and wrongly implied a story about Fulgrim and Isstvan V. The actual story is a Great Crusade campaign on One-Five-Four Four (later Caldera) against the Eldar, who abduct Ferrus Manus into a psychic labyrinth to try to divert him from his fate; the human counterpoint is Bion Henricos and the founding of the Chainveil. Legions expanded: the Salamanders and Death Guard are on-world in the same campaign per the Black Library story description, and the Imperial Army auxiliaries are central to the resolution. The Eldar are the antagonists, but the site has no existing Eldar or Aeldari faction tag, so they are described in the blurb rather than added as a new tag. Timeline left at 001.M31 but flagged: no source consulted gives a year for the One-Five-Four Four campaign, only that it is mid-Great Crusade, so the existing value is unverified rather than known-wrong.

entries.title: THE KABAN PROJECT
entries.notes: Confirmed as Mechanicum, so that faction tag was already right. The blurb was wrong on substance: it describes the story as set during the Mechanicum's civil war, which it predates, and names no protagonist. The story follows Adept Third Class Pallas Ravachol, the machine is a commission from Horus, and Urtzi Malevolus is separately building the Warmaster's Terminator armour. Timeline of 003-004.M31 left unchanged; sources place it in the early stages of the Heresy and before the events of the novel Mechanicum, but give no year.

entries.title: THE LIGHTNING TOWER
entries.notes: Confirmed: Dorn and Malcador on Terra. Legions corrected from 'Imperial Palace', which is a location rather than a faction, to Imperial Fists. Format confirmed as a print short story, first published in the 2007 Games Day Horus Heresy Chapbook; the Black Library audio release is a narration of it. The manifest blurb described siege preparation only and missed the substance of the piece, which is the repeated question 'what are you afraid of' and the Lightning Tower card from Curze's deck.

entries.title: THE REFLECTION CRACK'D
entries.notes: The manifest blurb had the story backwards. It claims the daemon claims full control and that Fulgrim becomes a Daemon Prince of Slaanesh; in fact Fulgrim has already reversed the possession and trapped the daemon in the painting, and his daemonhood comes much later in the series. Faction and type were already correct. The viewpoint character is Lucius, not Fulgrim.

entries.title: RAVEN'S FLIGHT
entries.notes: Format correction. This was the first original Horus Heresy audio drama, written by Gav Thorpe, performed by Toby Longworth and directed by Lisa Bowerman, released on CD in February 2010; it only appeared in print two years later in Shadows of Treachery. Labelling it a Short Story hides that. Legions expanded: the Iron Warriors and World Eaters are the on-page enemies, and the Marcus Valerius thread with the Imperial Army auxiliaries is half the story and was entirely missing from the manifest blurb. The date 006.M31 is stated on the Lexicanum page itself.

entries.title: THE SHARDS OF EREBUS
entries.notes: The manifest blurb inverted the chronology. It describes the aftermath of Calth with Ultramarines hunting Erebus for vengeance; the story is set immediately before the ambush and is told entirely from the Word Bearers side. The Wordaholic Anonymous review independently confirms that it takes place before Know No Fear and consists of Word Bearers receiving shards of a blade from Erebus. Ultramarines removed from the faction list: they are the intended victims, discussed at the council of war, but they never appear.

entries.title: THE LION
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was invented and describes a completely different story, a running duel between the Lion and Konrad Curze; that is Savage Weapons and Prince of Crows, not this novella. The Black Library description is explicit: 'Fighting a daemonic incursion within their fleet, the Dark Angels stumble into a conflict between the Iron Hands and Death Guard.' Legions corrected accordingly, which adds a traitor Legion (Death Guard) and a second loyalist one (Iron Hands) to what had been tagged as a Dark Angels-only story. Timeline left at 007-009.M31, matching Lexicanum's dating of the Thramas Crusade; the novella sits shortly before Prince of Crows.

entries.title: THE SERPENT BENEATH
entries.notes: Type, faction and date were already right. The manifest blurb was pure atmosphere and described no events at all, and it mistakenly treats Alpharius Omegon as a single undifferentiated figure; the whole point of the novella is Omegon acting separately from, and arguably against, Alpharius. The faction list is kept to Alpha Legion: the White Scars are the subject of the station's work but never appear on the page.

entries.title: THE CRIMSON FIST
entries.notes: Broadly right in the manifest, but sharpened. The fleet is stranded by warp storms rather than lured into 'Perturabo's trap'; the Iron Warriors locate it via a psi-array planted in the system. The Sigismund and Dorn thread on Terra is roughly half the novella and was missing entirely. Iron Warriors added to the faction list. Date confirmed: Lexicanum gives the Battle of Phall as 007.M31.

entries.title: CALTH THAT WAS
entries.notes: Format correction: this is the novella of Mark of Calth, not a short story. Lexicanum states the anthology contains 'seven short stories by various authors, and one novella by Graham McNeill'; the Warhammer 40k Wiki page is titled and categorised as a novella; and the Black Library back-cover copy calls it 'the novella-length Calth That Was'. The Wordaholic Anonymous review also notes it is by far the longest piece in the book. Word Bearers added to the faction list. Confidence is medium on plot detail because no source consulted carries a scene-level summary, so the blurb stays close to the two published synopses and adds nothing beyond them.

entries.title: DARK HEART
entries.notes: Faction, type and date were already right, and the manifest named Marduk correctly. Sharpened because the manifest framed it as 'the XVII Legion's perspective on the betrayal' and a straightforward rise through the ranks; the published description is explicit that Marduk's target is not the Ultramarines but rivals inside his own Legion. The Wordaholic Anonymous review adds the specific hook, that Marduk has to account for having left his mentor for dead. Medium confidence: no scene-level summary exists on either wiki.

entries.title: THE TRAVELLER
entries.notes: The weakest-sourced entry in the batch. Both wikis carry only the one-line Black Library synopsis: 'A survivor of the Word Bearers' initial surprise attack on the orbital defences of Calth finds that he may not be alone.' The Wordaholic Anonymous review supplies the setting and register, that it follows ordinary people in the underground arcologies and is 'man vs his own mental well being vs deamonic onslaught'. Nothing beyond those two sources has been asserted, and the viewpoint character is not named in either, so mainCharacters is left empty. The manifest's claim that he 'wanders Calth's poisoned surface' after an orbital bombardment is unsupported: he is a survivor of the attack on the orbital defence platforms and the action is underground. Word Bearers added to the factions; the Ultramarines tag is retained for the Ultramar setting rather than for a Space Marine viewpoint, which this story does not have.

entries.title: A DEEPER DARKNESS
entries.notes: Factions, type and date were already right and the manifest named both characters correctly. Corrected because the manifest reduces it to a cat-and-mouse chase and drops the actual point, which both published synopses state plainly: Pelion realises there are things in the warp that even the Word Bearers should fear. The Wordaholic Anonymous review independently confirms Pelion's rank as sergeant, the obsessive nature of the hunt, and the gothic-horror register.

entries.title: THE UNDERWORLD WAR
entries.notes: Timeline correction, and the clearest date error in the batch. Both wikis state the story is set seven standard years after the Battle of Calth. Lexicanum dates the Battle of Calth to 007.M31 and notes the underground war continues until 014.M31, so the story sits at 014.M31, not the manifest's 007-009.M31. The manifest blurb otherwise had the gist right; it has been rewritten to include the Argel Tal and Gal Vorbak material, which the Wordaholic Anonymous review confirms is the core of the piece, and the deliberate ambiguity between past and future.

entries.title: UNMARKED
entries.notes: Faction, type and date were already right, and the manifest correctly named Verdun and 73 Easting. Rewritten because it omitted the actual premise: this is a direct continuation of Know No Fear in which Oll uses the athame from John French's story to cut warp portals, travelling with a band of Calth survivors and pursued by the daemon M'kar. The faction stays as Perpetuals rather than adding Word Bearers, since M'kar appears as a daemon rather than as a Legion force.

entries.title: PRINCE OF CROWS
entries.notes: Type and date were right; Lexicanum's plot summary opens '009.M31, Sheol'. The manifest blurb was broadly in the right area but vague and slightly off, describing 'the Lion's relentless pursuit' when the novella actually opens with Curze already beaten and comatose. Dark Angels added to the factions: the I Legion are the on-page antagonists throughout and the novella ends aboard the Invincible Reason. A Raven Guard captain, Alastor Rushal, also serves on the Kyroptera, but he is not enough of a presence to warrant a Raven Guard tag.

entries.title: PROMETHEAN SUN
entries.notes: Great Crusade story, not a Heresy one. Set on the world One-Five-Four Four (the same campaign as the novella Feat of Iron, which this database also dates 001.M31, so the existing timeline is consistent and left unchanged). Current legions listed only Salamanders; the Lexicanum cover description explicitly has the Iron Hands under Ferrus Manus and the Death Guard under Mortarion fighting the same war. The eldar are the antagonists but the site has no canonical Aeldari faction value, so they are described in the blurb rather than added to legions. I deliberately did not repeat 40kTimeline's claim that the Emperor walks the campaign, as no primary-sourced page supports it. Type Novella and timeline 001.M31 both confirmed.

entries.title: IMMORTAL DUTY
entries.notes: REPRINT. This is the same story as bookKey flame-immortal-duty-2 (L.5) in this batch; both copies have been given identical corrected text. It also appears in the Meduson and Lupercal's War anthologies. Serious faction error corrected: both database copies said Salamanders, but the story is Iron Hands. The Black Library blurb on Lexicanum names Ahrem Gallikus, a Medusan Immortal and disgraced warrior of the Iron Hands, and both The Heresy Reviewed and PurpleHeresy independently describe it as an Iron Hands versus World Eaters boarding action above Isstvan V told in flashback. Timeline 006.M31 and type Short Story confirmed.

entries.title: SCORCHED EARTH
entries.notes: The current blurb's 'wage war across scorched worlds' was wrong: this is a single, tightly bounded story on the Isstvan V battlefield itself. Named protagonists Ra'stan and Usabius come from the Lexicanum cover description; the added legions come from that page's dramatis personae, which lists Iron Hands (Erasmus Ruuman, Ishmal Sulnar, Tarkan), Raven Guard (Morvax Haukspeer) and Emperor's Children (Lorimarr). Type Novella and timeline 006.M31 confirmed.

entries.title: SONS OF THE FORGE
entries.notes: The prior audit's flag is confirmed. The protagonist is Forgefather T'kell, not Numeon, and the Black Library blurb reproduced on Lexicanum names T'kell explicitly. Lexicanum's T'kell article, citing Sons of the Forge chapter three, states the journey begins 'when Artellus Numeon returned Vulkan's body to Nocturne', which is the end of Deathfire, so Numeon is dead before the novella's main action. Timeline moved from 006.M31 to 010.M31 to match this database's own dating of Deathfire (010.M31) and Old Earth (011.M31), between which the novella sits. Legions expanded from Salamanders alone using the Lexicanum dramatis personae: Iron Hands (Kastigan Ulok, Ahrem Gallikus), Sons of Horus (Vosto Kurnan) and Dark Mechanicum (Regulus). One Raven Guard warrior, Morikan, also appears but is too minor to list. Note that the Born of Flame cover copy calls this 'the novel Sons of the Forge' while Black Library and Lexicanum both classify it as a novella at 204 pages; Novella retained.

entries.title: ARTEFACTS
entries.notes: REPRINT. This story also exists elsewhere in this database as bookKey war-artefacts (XXXIII.8, the War Without End anthology, also dated 006.M31); that copy is outside this batch and should be given this same corrected text. The story additionally appears in Sedition's Gate and Lupercal's War. The current blurb ('recover precious relics from the war's devastation') was a title paraphrase and factually backwards: nothing is recovered, Vulkan orders his armoury destroyed. Lexicanum carries a full scene-by-scene plot summary. Legions left as Salamanders only: Curze and the Night Lords feature heavily but purely in Vulkan's recollection, and adding them would wrongly flip a traitor filter. This is the direct set-up for Sons of the Forge. Type and timeline confirmed.

entries.title: IMMORTAL DUTY
entries.notes: REPRINT. Identical story to bookKey shattered-immortal-duty (XLIII.3) in this batch; both copies deliberately carry the same corrected text. Also collected in Meduson and Lupercal's War. Same serious correction as the other copy: Salamanders replaced with Iron Hands and World Eaters. Ahrem Gallikus is also listed among the Shattered Legions characters in the Sons of the Forge dramatis personae, which corroborates his Iron Hands identity.

entries.title: UNFORGED
entries.notes: Faction corrected from Iron Hands to Salamanders. Lexicanum's Meduson anthology page summarises Unforged as 'an examination of the broken nature of the Salamanders', and three independent reviews agree: The Heresy Reviewed has the Strike and Fade characters ambushed by their own oblivious battle-brothers, Speculiction describes untested Salamanders investigating a homing beacon in a ravine, and PurpleHeresy names the returning cast Jo'Phor, Hae'Phast and the mute Donak. Strike and Fade is itself a Salamanders story (survivors ambushing Night Lords on Isstvan V), so both sides of the friendly-fire incident are Salamanders and no other Legion is listed. Type and timeline unchanged; 007.M31 fits 'long after the Dropsite Massacre'. Directly continued by Unspoken.

entries.title: GREY TALON
entries.notes: Serious faction error corrected. There are no Raven Guard in this story at all; the current entry appears to have guessed from the word 'Talon'. Lexicanum carries a full scene-by-scene plot summary and its Shadrak Meduson article cites the story independently. Correct factions are Iron Hands (Bion Henricos), White Scars (Hibou Khan and the sagyar mazan penitents, following the schism in Scars) and Sons of Horus as the enemy. The ship was originally seized at Isstvan V by Salamanders who renamed her Hesiod, but they had been replaced by the White Scars before the story opens, so Salamanders are not listed. Type Audio Drama confirmed (prose in Meduson 2015, MP3 January 2016); timeline 007.M31 unchanged, consistent with this database's dating of Scars.

entries.title: MEDUSON
entries.notes: The prior audit's flag is confirmed: this is Shadrak Meduson's origin story. Timeline corrected from 008-011.M31 to 006.M31. Lexicanum's Meduson article, citing this story throughout, places all of it in the immediate aftermath of Isstvan V: the boarding of the Ironside, DuCaine's death signal, the Clan Fathers taking collective command, Jebez Aug being made Warleader with Meduson as his Hand Elect, the Sons of Horus ambush that destroys the Crown of Flame, and Meduson finally taking the warleadership and vowing to take Tybalt Marr's head. Sons of Horus added as the antagonist faction. Salamanders and Raven Guard survivors are folded into Clan Sorrgol during the story but are not viewpoint factions, so they are not listed. Type Short Story confirmed.

entries.title: THE KEYS OF HEL
entries.notes: The prior audit's flag is confirmed as Iron Hands, but the current blurb badly misread the title: the Keys of Hel are not a weapon the Shattered Legions go hunting for, they are seals Ferrus Manus placed on forbidden Dark Age and xenos technologies, and turning them is what some Iron Hands do to themselves. Salamanders and Raven Guard removed; the enemy is the Death Guard, per The Heresy Reviewed's per-story summary. Lexicanum's Keys of Hel article cites this story for cybernetic resurrection, several of the named forbidden technologies, and Soter of Clan Kadoran as a revenant. Crius's return is confirmed by PurpleHeresy and by his own Lexicanum article, which ends Riven with him reanimated. Type and timeline unchanged.

entries.title: DEEDS ENDURE
entries.notes: Serious faction error corrected: there are no Raven Guard in this story. Lexicanum's Meduson anthology page carries the full Black Library blurb, which names Salamanders and Iron Hands who have found common cause and a World Eaters force among a civilian population. The Heresy Reviewed and PurpleHeresy both independently describe the same set-up, PurpleHeresy specifying a World Eaters training facility and the orbital-bombardment argument. No named protagonist could be established from any source, so mainCharacters is left empty rather than invented. Type and timeline unchanged.

entries.title: THE NOOSE
entries.notes: The current blurb's 'traitor supply lines' was invented. This is a ship-to-ship duel. Four independent sources agree it is Iron Hands versus Emperor's Children: Lexicanum's one-line summary, Track of Words ('a cat and mouse game of traps and bluffs'), Speculiction and The Heresy Reviewed, the last of which names Captain Khalybus and the closing ambush. Emperor's Children added to legions. Type and timeline unchanged. PurpleHeresy notes the tonal debt to the Iron Hands versus Emperor's Children void war in The Damnation of Pythos, but no source calls it a direct sequel, so that link is not asserted.

entries.title: UNSPOKEN
entries.notes: The current blurb was pure title paraphrase. Salamanders and Alpha Legion added. Lexicanum records only that Unspoken continues Unforged, which is a Salamanders story; The Heresy Reviewed supplies the mixed Iron Hands and Salamanders force, the mute survivor viewpoint, the astropathic relay station and the Alpha Legion infiltrators; PurpleHeresy independently names the protagonist Donak and confirms Tarkan and Sulnar carry over from Nick Kyme's Scorched Earth; Speculiction independently confirms the first-person Salamander narrator who ends up switching Legions. Type and timeline unchanged.

entries.title: THE EITHER
entries.notes: Serious faction error corrected. This is a traitor-viewpoint story: the protagonist is Sons of Horus Captain Tybalt Marr, per the Black Library blurb on Lexicanum, Track of Words and The Heresy Reviewed. Listing it as Iron Hands only would put a Sons of Horus story on the wrong side of a loyalist filter, so Sons of Horus is listed first with Iron Hands retained as the opposing faction. Timeline moved from 010.M31 to 006-009.M31: the story replays the events of Meduson (006.M31) from Marr's perspective and ends on Dwell just after the assassination attempt on Horus, which this database dates via Vengeful Spirit to 008-009.M31, so 010.M31 is too late. Confidence marked medium for the date only; the faction correction is high confidence. Type Audio Drama confirmed.

entries.title: THE HAND ELECT
entries.notes: The current blurb was a generic title paraphrase. The Hand Elect is a specific rank, Meduson's second-in-command, and the story is about one man: Jebez Aug. The Black Library blurb on Lexicanum states it is 'the tale of how Jebez Aug, the Hand Elect of Warleader Shadrak Meduson, sought out the aid of the Mechanicus to restore him of his wounds and what it cost him'; The Heresy Reviewed adds the loyalist forge world and the scheming to replace Meduson. Mechanicum added to legions. Note this story was added only for the 2016 Ultimate Edition of Meduson and Lexicanum files it as 'Hand Elect' without the article, but the Shattered Legions contents page uses 'The Hand Elect', which is kept. Timeline left at 010.M31: Aug's wounds date from Meduson (006.M31) but the internal politicking points forward to the Cult of the Gorgon arc resolved in Old Earth (011.M31), and no source fixes the date, so the existing value was not disturbed.

entries.title: THE SEVENTH SERPENT
entries.notes: Raven Guard and Salamanders added: the Sisypheum's crew is a mixed Shattered Legions band, per the Black Library synopsis and Track of Words, which names Wayland and Sharrowkin. Lexicanum's Shadrak Meduson and Cadmus Tyro articles both cite this novella for the key reveal, that Alpharius impersonated Meduson and was exposed by Tyro's force, which is why the blurb states it rather than the softer 'Meduson orchestrated it' framing on the cover copy. Type Novella and timeline 011.M31 both left unchanged: the story follows the Sisypheum's escape from Iydris in Angel Exterminatus but Lexicanum places the impersonation in the post-Dwell period, so anything from roughly 009.M31 to just before Old Earth is defensible and the existing value sits inside that window.

entries.title: THE SOLAR WAR
entries.notes: Official Black Library synopsis (Fandom series page) and the Track of Words review agree: this is the void war for the Sol System, not the assault on Terra itself. Original blurb's 'traitor fleets arrive at Terra' understated the system-wide scope, so reframed. Track of Words confirms the viewpoint cast (Dorn, Sigismund, Abaddon, Mersadie Oliton, Admiral Su-Kassen, Ahriman). Legions left untouched: Imperial Fists and Sons of Horus are firmly confirmed, but I could not source Iron Warriors participation specifically in this volume, so it is flagged rather than removed. Date 014.M31 left alone (the Fandom chronology dates the wider Solar War 007-015.M31, with the Terra phase in 014.M31).

entries.title: THE LOST AND THE DAMNED
entries.notes: Original blurb was broadly right on theme but vague on mechanics. Track of Words confirms the aegis shield is the barrier Horus must first break, that conscript Katsuhiro is the human throughline, and that the cast includes Dorn, Sanguinius, the Khan, Malcador, Valdor, Raldoron, Thane, Abaddon, Zardu Layak, the Night Lords and Legio Solaria. Official synopsis names Mortarion's plague weapons and Angron's fury. Replaced the vague 'All Traitor Legions' with the specific legions the sources evidence. The original line 'daemon engines and corrupted Titans pour onto the Throneworld' was dropped as unsupported emphasis; the title refers to the mortal levies Horus throws at the guns. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: THE FIRST WALL
entries.notes: Direction of the Lion's Gate assault verified as correct in the original blurb: Track of Words states Perturabo tasks Warsmith Kroeger with taking the space port, with the Imperial Fists under Fafnir Rann defending. The Saturnine review confirms the port has fallen by the following book. Removed 'master siege-breaker faces master fortifier' as it implies a personal Dorn versus Perturabo clash that does not happen here; Perturabo directs, Kroeger and Forrix carry the narrative. Added the two secondary threads (Custodian Amon Tauromachian and Zenobi Adedeji of Addaba Hive) that the review identifies as a third of the book. Zenobi's regiment's purpose deliberately left unstated to avoid spoiling it.

entries.title: SATURNINE
entries.notes: Two genuine factual errors fixed. First, the original called the Saturnine gambit 'Horus's desperate strike at the Saturnine Wall'. It is Dorn's gambit, not Horus's: the official synopsis states 'Dorn simply cannot defend everything' and the Track of Words review describes Dorn facing impossible questions of compromise and sacrifice as he searches for a strategy to tip his battle of wills with Perturabo. Second, the original claimed 'one of the twin Primarchs meets their end' here. Alpharius was slain by Rogal Dorn at the Battle of Pluto in 010.M31, four years earlier, in the events of Praetorian of Dorn, per both the Battle of Pluto page and the Horus Heresy Chronology. That claim was both wrong and a false spoiler, so it is gone. Legions: swapped Alpha Legion for Iron Warriors, as Perturabo is the confirmed opposing commander and I could find no source for an Alpha Legion role in this volume. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: MORTIS
entries.notes: Three corrections. The original placed the Titan battles 'across Terra's wastelands'; the official synopsis is specific that the clash is at the Mercury Wall, Legio Mortis against Legio Ignatum. The original listed Death Guard as a featured faction and named Mortarion; neither appears in the official synopsis and I found no source for a Death Guard role here, so Death Guard is replaced with the two named Titan Legios. The original claim 'Time itself begins to break down' is unsupported and was dropped; the actual metaphysical thread is the false-paradise dreams and the search for a way to turn back the Warp's influence. Legio Ignatum's Fandom page independently confirms it as the loyalist Titan Legion defending the Palace and the sworn rival of Legio Mortis. Confidence is medium rather than high only because mainCharacters could not be sourced beyond Horus: no source I could reach names the individual princeps viewpoint characters, so the list is deliberately minimal rather than invented. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: WARHAWK
entries.notes: The original framed the book purely as a Khan versus Mortarion duel and asserted 'The Khan must defeat Mortarion or Terra falls'. The official synopsis is explicit that the objective is the liberation of the Lion's Gate space port, with Mortarion as the enemy standing in the way, so the objective is now stated. Added the two arcs the official synopsis names and the original omitted: the black sword forged from spite (Sigismund, hence Imperial Fists added to legions) and the saint and sinner released into the ruins. Track of Words independently confirms this as the culmination of the White Scars versus Death Guard arc and names Ilya Ravallion as a key viewpoint. Softened the safe summary, which previously announced the duel outright as 'the ultimate duel between speed and endurance'; it now describes the mission and the stakes without promising the confrontation or its result. Also removed the em dash present in the original. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: ECHOES OF ETERNITY
entries.notes: Two unsourced claims removed from the full blurb: 'Sanguinius defeats Angron, banishing him to the Warp' and 'The Great Angel's wings are broken'. Neither could be verified from any source I could reach; the Fandom Angron and Sanguinius pages still carry the older pre-Siege-series account (Ka'Bandha at the Eternity Gate) and were not usable. What is verifiable is that Sanguinius successfully defended the Eternity Gate, per the Fandom Imperial Palace page, so the blurb now says the Gate holds at cost and stops there. Track of Words independently confirms the tight focus on the battle for the Eternity Gate, on Sanguinius and Angron and their Legions, and the supporting cast of Zephon, Lotara Sarrin, Arkhan Land, Amit and Kargos Bloodspitter; the Zephon page corroborates the Gorgon Bar, Arkhan Land and Eternity Gate threads. Safe summary rewritten from the official Black Library synopsis: the original nudged at Sanguinius 'seeing visions of what may come', which foreshadows his fate, and that is gone. Confidence medium because the precise outcome of the Sanguinius and Angron confrontation remains unsourced and is therefore not asserted.

entries.title: THE END AND THE DEATH: VOLUME I
entries.notes: The original said the boarding party 'teleport to the flagship but are scattered across the ship' in this volume. Track of Words describes volume one as setting everything up for the endgame, with the Emperor rising only at the close, which matches the official synopsis wording 'at the final hour of the final day, the Emperor rises'. The scattering aboard the Vengeful Spirit is a later-volume event, so it is removed. The original also listed only the Emperor, Sanguinius and Dorn; the official synopsis is 'His Angel, His Praetorian, and His Captain', the Captain being Loken, who the original omitted. Track of Words confirms the viewpoint cast of Sanguinius, Malcador (heavily), Fafnir Rann, Loken, Keeler, Sindermann, Oll Persson and John Grammaticus, plus rare Horus POV scenes. Legions left as 'All Legions', which is accurate for the finale.

entries.title: THE END AND THE DEATH: VOLUME II
entries.notes: Full blurb kept its substance and is accurate: Sanguinius boarding the Vengeful Spirit to kill Horus is the official Black Library synopsis for this volume, and the Volume III synopsis opens by confirming 'The Great Angel, Sanguinius, lies slain at his brother Horus's hand'. Track of Words confirms the enormous supporting cast (Horus, Dorn, Sanguinius, Loken, Sindermann, Keeler, Fo, Abaddon, Amit, Fafnir Rann, Sigismund, Oll Persson). Safe summary rewritten: the original said Sanguinius confronts Horus 'knowing what fate may await him', which telegraphs the biggest death in the setting. It is now the official spoiler-free framing, which states the intent and the stakes but not the result.

entries.title: THE END AND THE DEATH: VOLUME III
entries.notes: One unsourced specific removed: the original stated 'When Horus strikes down Ollanius Pius, the Emperor accepts His son is beyond redemption'. The Fandom Siege of Terra page is explicit that the identity of the warrior who interposed himself is disputed in-universe, with Ollanius Pius being the Adeptus Ministorum's version, and I could not source what actually happens on that beat in this volume, so it is gone. Also removed 'Dorn finds his father dying', which I could not source. What is retained is verified: the Volume III official synopsis supplies Malcador ablaze on the Golden Throne, the Dark Angels holding the Hollow Mountain with Keeler's pilgrims against Typhus, reality unravelling, and Guilliman racing for Terra. The Fandom Siege of Terra and Legio Ignatum pages both confirm the Emperor slays Horus and obliterates his soul, at the cost of His own body and permanent interment in the Golden Throne. Safe summary softened: the original said the Emperor 'must decide if his son can be redeemed and what price victory will demand', which strongly telegraphs the ending, and it also carried an em dash. It now states the situation and stops at the meeting. Legions left as 'All Legions'; the sources would support adding Dark Angels and Death Guard, left for a human to decide for consistency across the three volumes.

entries.title: CHILD OF NIGHT
entries.notes: Manifest legion tag of Knights-Errant was wrong: this is a Night Lords story with no Knights-Errant named in any source. The hunter stalking Zharost is unnamed in Lexicanum's summary, so I have not attributed him to a faction. In-universe date could not be verified from any source; manifest value left as is, though the story must post-date the VIII Legion's open treachery.

entries.title: WOLF HUNT
entries.notes: Nothing to do with the Space Wolves. It is the direct sequel to The Outcast Dead and follows Severian of the Luna Wolves being hunted on Terra by Yasu Nagasena. Legion tag change flips this from loyalist (Space Wolves) to traitor (Luna Wolves) on the site filter, which is correct for the Legion featured even though Severian himself is an outcast later recruited by Malcador. Knights-Errant retained for the unseen third party directing the hunt. Type: the author's own site, the Warhammer 40k Wiki and Grimdark Archive all call it a full-cast audio drama (1h15, cast of performers). Lexicanum's page is titled 'Audio Book', which is probably where the manifest value came from.

entries.title: THE WATCHER
entries.notes: The prior audit was right. No Dark Angels and no Watchers in the Dark. Lexicanum names the Knight-Errant as Ison, a former Legion Librarian; the Black Library blurb describes the story as revealing what happened to those sent to watch over the Night Haunter, and the Goodreads entry names the Space Wolves watch-pack sent to watch the Night Lords. Legion change removes a loyalist Legion that never appears and adds a traitor Legion that does. In-universe date not verifiable; manifest value retained.

entries.title: GREY ANGEL
entries.notes: Manifest blurb was generic. Concrete plot confirmed by three sources: Loken and Qruze on Caliban, captured by Luther, aided out by Cypher and a Watcher in the Dark. Dark Angels added to legions (loyalist, so no traitor-filter flip). Type corrected to Audio Drama: it was released on CD as an audio drama alongside Swallow's Burden of Duty, per Track of Words and purpleheresy; Lexicanum's page title says Audio Book. Timeline narrowed to 008.M31 because this is Loken's first Knight-Errant mission, after Garro: Legion of One (008.M31 in this dataset) and before Luna Mendax and Vengeful Spirit (008-009.M31).

entries.title: LUNA MENDAX
entries.notes: The prior audit was right: this is Loken's recovery on Luna, not deception spreading across Luna. Lexicanum explicitly describes the visitor as the spirit of Tarik Torgaddon, slain months earlier on Isstvan III, and the story ending with Qruze bringing Malcador's summons. Legions changed from Various to Knights-Errant. Timeline narrowed to 008.M31, placing it after Grey Angel and immediately before Vengeful Spirit (008-009.M31 in this dataset).

entries.title: THE PURGE
entries.notes: Not a Death Guard story at all. It is Anthony Reynolds' Word Bearers novella following Sor Talgron, with a Terra strand featuring Rogal Dorn and an Ultramar strand against the Ultramarines' 17th Chapter. Legion tag stays traitor-side but changes traitor Legion. Timeline widened to 006-008.M31 on Lexicanum's in-universe dates: 132006.M31 for Talgron's arrival at the Imperial Palace and 454008.M31 for the end of the Percepton Primus campaign. Custodian Guard (Tiber Acanthus) and Nathaniel Garro also appear but only in passing, so I left them off the faction list.

entries.title: GHOSTS SPEAK NOT
entries.notes: Not a Garro story. The protagonist is Amendera Kendel, former Sister of Silence and Malcador's Agentia Tertius. Track of Words places it in the Proxima system; Lexicanum confirms Kendel recruiting Helig Gallor from the Seventy. Caution on the site filter: the Death Guard here are the loyalist Eisenstein survivors, so a crude traitor-filter will mark this entry traitor-side when the XIV Legion warriors in it are loyal.

entries.title: ARMY OF ONE
entries.notes: Verified against the full text of the story itself, which is roughly 1,000 words. Not a Knights-Errant story: the protagonist is an Eversor Assassin of the Officio Assassinorum, named Ganimus by Malcador. Track of Words tags it Officio Assassinorum and the Black Library blurb describes Malcador despatching a living weapon to Proxima Apocryphis. In-universe date not stated anywhere; manifest value retained.

entries.title: DISTANT ECHOES OF OLD NIGHT
entries.notes: Nothing to do with Old Night or ancient horrors resurfacing, and no Knights-Errant. It is a Death Guard versus Imperial Fists skirmish story led by Chaplain Morgax Murnau with a Destroyer squad. Track of Words and Lexicanum both give the same core, purpleheresy adds the moon's name, Algonquis. Legion change flips this entry from a neutral Knights-Errant tag to traitor-side (Death Guard) plus loyalist Imperial Fists. In-universe date not sourced; manifest value retained.

entries.title: LOST SONS
entries.notes: Not Garro recruiting from traitor Legions. It is the Blood Angels garrison left on Baal, told through Warden Arkad, visited by the Knight-Errant Tylos Rubio. All three sources agree. Timeline: Lexicanum and purpleheresy both put the story roughly five years after the Legion departed for Signus, which in this dataset (Fear to Tread at 005-006.M31) works out at about 010-011.M31 rather than the manifest's 009.M31. Confidence medium on that date only, since it is derived rather than quoted.

entries.title: TEMPLAR
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was roughly right about Sigismund but the legion tag said Knights-Errant, which is wrong and hides a traitor Legion. Lexicanum gives the setting as a comet-shrine dedicated to Unity, with Word Bearers trying to work their way back into the Solar System; Track of Words confirms the mission to cleanse a Word Bearers enclave. Sigismund is not the Emperor's Champion at this point, he is First Captain. In-universe date not sourced; manifest value retained, though Track of Words describes the piece as showing him early in the Heresy.

entries.title: PATIENCE
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was a paraphrase of the title. The protagonist is Helig Gallor, not Garro, and the story is a micro-short set on Nolec Trinus. Track of Words and Lexicanum agree on Gallor searching for Garro; Lexicanum supplies the world's name and the daemon that regenerates from blood and corpses. Legions tag of Knights-Errant is correct and unchanged. Both leads are ex-Death Guard, but they act as Knights-Errant here, so I did not add the XIV Legion and trip the traitor filter. Faction list reconciled with the live data after the allegiance override was added, so a correct tag no longer has to be withheld to protect the filter.

entries.title: THE SIGILLITE
entries.notes: Despite the title this is not a story about Malcador orchestrating a shadow war. It is a baseline human viewpoint story: Track of Words and the Black Library blurb both name Captain Khalid Hassan of the Fourth Clandestine Orta, returning from Gyptus to be debriefed by Malcador, with no Astartes protagonist. Lexicanum's page body names the officer 'Hasani Sabbyat', which conflicts with two other sources, so I went with Khalid Hassan; worth a second look if precision on the name matters. Legions changed from Knights-Errant (none appear) to Imperial Army. Type corrected to Audio Drama: Lexicanum's own page text calls it an original audio drama with three credited performers, even though the page is titled Audio Book. In-universe date not sourced; manifest value retained.

entries.title: THE GATES OF TERRA
entries.notes: Not Imperial Fists fortifying the Throneworld. The viewpoint character is Captain Arcadese of the Ultramarines, previously seen in Forgotten Sons, holding the Ardent Reef. Lexicanum repeats the deliberately misleading cover blurb about Horus's final assault; purpleheresy gives the actual twist, that the battle is a psychically implanted simulation run by Malcador's and Dorn's Librarians as battle-conditioning before the real Siege, which Track of Words corroborates in describing the story as ambiguous and about how far loyalist commanders will go. Confidence medium because only one source states the twist outright. In-universe date not sourced; manifest value retained, and it is at least consistent with the story sitting before the Siege.

entries.title: THE LAST CHURCH
entries.notes: Facts in the existing entry were already correct, so this is a wording tightening rather than a correction. Added the priest's name (Uriah Olathaire), the church's name (Church of the Lightning Stone) and the Emperor's alias (Revelation). Timeline left unchanged but flagged: Lexicanum dates the end of the Unification Wars to 712.M30 and says the last church was destroyed 'shortly before the Great Crusade' (which begins circa 798.M30), so 730.M30 may be a decade or more too early. No source gives an exact year. The 'Emperor' faction tag is not a canonical faction name but it is retained because it is the site's existing loyalist tag for this entry.

entries.title: AFTER DESH'EA
entries.notes: Existing entry was substantially accurate. Corrected detail: Khârn does not 'arrive with the War Hounds' to find Angron, he is one of a succession of officers sent into the hold, and he is the only one to survive the encounter. The Legion is still named War Hounds during the story and is renamed World Eaters at its close, so the World Eaters faction tag is right. Timeline 899.M30 kept but unverified: neither Lexicanum's Angron page nor the story page gives an in-universe year for his discovery.

entries.title: WOLF AT THE DOOR
entries.notes: The previous blurb was generic Space Wolves flavour text with no actual plot. The Legion guess happened to be right, but the story is specifically Bulveye's 13th Great Company against Dark Eldar, and the Dark Eldar were missing entirely from the faction list. Setting is Antimon (Lexicanum also lists Kernunnos in the same subsector). Timeline 950.M30 kept but unverified: sources place it in the Great Crusade with the 954th Expedition Fleet and give no year.

entries.title: SCIONS OF THE STORM
entries.notes: Previous blurb was invented. The real story is Sor Talgron at Forty-Seven Sixteen, the same world covered in The First Heretic. Timeline changed because 956.M30 predates the razing of Monarchia (962.M30), and both Lexicanum and The Heresy Reviewed place this story AFTER Kor Phaeron and Erebus have turned Lorgar against the Emperor but before the rank-and-file Word Bearers are corrupted, i.e. shortly after Monarchia. The 962-965.M30 range is derived from The First Heretic's own dating rather than stated outright anywhere, so a human should sanity-check it. Faction list unchanged: only the Word Bearers feature as a Legion (a Custodian detachment under Aquillon is attached to the Legion at this point but its presence in this specific story is unconfirmed).

entries.title: CALL OF THE LION
entries.notes: Significant error in the previous blurb: it claimed the story is set 'during the Heresy' and involves answering the Lion's summons. It is a Great Crusade story and the Lion does not appear. The real subject is the Terran versus Calibanite rift in the I Legion, personified by Astelan and Belath at Byzanthis, and it sets up Astelan's role in Fallen Angels. Timeline 960.M30 kept but unverified, no source gives a year.

entries.title: REBIRTH
entries.notes: Previous entry was pure fabrication: an abstract 'transformation and renewal' summary with faction 'Various'. The story is Thousand Sons versus World Eaters in the ruins of Tizca on Prospero, and it is the introduction of Revuel Arvida, whose survival is the seed of the Blood Ravens. Faction change from 'Various' to two named Legions will alter loyalist/traitor filtering. Timeline 004-005.M31 retained as consistent with the Burning of Prospero.

entries.title: BLOOD GAMES
entries.notes: Previous entry was close but incomplete. Corrections: the Blood Game is an infiltration exercise against the Palace rather than a year-long deployment (no source supports 'year-long'), Hy Brasil is a Terran continental realm not a set of hives, the named suspect is Lord Pherom Sichar, and the resolution is that he is not the traitor he appears to be. Constantin Valdor and Rogal Dorn both appear, hence adding Imperial Fists. Timeline 006.M31 retained: sources place it on Terra after the Isstvan III atrocity.

entries.title: THE VOICE
entries.notes: Worst faction record in the batch: the Legion field read 'Audio', which is a format label, not a faction. This is a Sisters of Silence story and there are no Space Marines in it. The previous blurb was invented from the title ('the power of voice and influence'). Timeline is the weak point: 006.M31 is retained but the plot turns on a warning that could end the Heresy 'before it begins', which suggests an earlier setting, possibly pre-Isstvan. No source gives a year, so a human should check. Amendera Kendel goes on to appear in Nemesis and later Siege material.

entries.title: THE FACE OF TREACHERY
entries.notes: Previous entry was fabricated from the title, an abstract essay on betrayal with faction 'Various'. The real story is the Raven Guard evacuation from Isstvan V, and it is a direct sequel to the Raven's Flight audio drama and a prequel to Deliverance Lost. Faction change from 'Various' to four named factions including both loyalist (Raven Guard, Imperial Army) and traitor (Alpha Legion, World Eaters) sides, so loyalist/traitor filtering will change materially. Format stays Short Story: it first appeared in print in Age of Darkness, and the 52-minute Jonathan Keeble recording is a later audiobook reading, not an originating audio drama.

entries.title: THE IRON WITHIN
entries.notes: This is the most consequential loyalty error in the batch. The previous blurb described the Iron Warriors as the attackers 'proving their cold brutality' for Perturabo. In fact the protagonist, Warsmith Barabas Dantioch, is a LOYALIST Iron Warrior who refuses to join the rebellion, and the besiegers are the traitor half of his own Legion. Ultramarines and Imperial Army forces fight on the loyalist side. Any filter that treats 'Iron Warriors' as automatically traitor will mislabel this story. Lexicanum also lists Sons of Horus among the forces present, omitted here as their role appears minor, worth a human check. Timeline 006-007.M31 retained and is consistent with a siege lasting roughly a year after the Legion declares for Horus.

entries.title: SAVAGE WEAPONS
entries.notes: Factions, format and timeline were already right. The plot description was wrong in shape: it is not a hunt or pursuit by the Lion, it is a parlay requested by Curze on Tsagualsa that degenerates into a duel, and Curze's precognition is not the driver. Adds the champions Corswain, Alajos, Sevatar and Sheng, and the introduction of Tsagualsa, which later Heresy fiction returns to repeatedly.

entries.title: RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
entries.notes: Previous blurb was a generic 'Ultramarines are rigid and doctrinaire' restatement of the title with no plot. The Legion tag was right. Faction list deliberately left as Ultramarines only: the Death Guard, World Eaters and Salamanders forces are simulated opponents rather than genuine belligerents, so tagging them would misrepresent the story, though a human may prefer to list them. This is also the story that first floats the Imperium Secundus idea. Timeline 008.M31 retained as consistent with Guilliman completing the Codex after Calth.

entries.title: LIAR'S DUE
entries.notes: Previous entry was invented from the title ('lies become weapons') with faction 'Various'. This is an Alpha Legion story told entirely from a civilian point of view, with no Space Marine combat, and the faction change from 'Various' to Alpha Legion moves it firmly onto the traitor side of any filter. Timeline 008.M31 retained, no source gives a year but a post-Isstvan setting where rumours of the Emperor's death are plausible fits.

entries.title: FORGOTTEN SONS
entries.notes: Previous blurb had the right Legion but invented the premise (Salamanders 'finding purpose' after being left behind). The story is a diplomatic mission to Bastion, and it is a two-hander: an Ultramarine, Arcadese, shares the lead with the Salamander Heka'tan, and an Iron Warrior is one of the two saboteurs, so both were missing from the faction list. Timeline 008.M31 retained but flagged: Lexicanum ties the story closely to the Isstvan V Dropsite Massacre, which would put it nearer 006-007.M31. No source gives a year.

entries.title: LITTLE HORUS
entries.notes: Previous blurb was thematically vague and missed the entire plot. Added the Battle of Dwell, the loyalist Shattered Legions force under Shadrak Meduson, the White Scars under Hibou Khan, the loss of Aximand's face and the Loken reveal. Iron Hands and White Scars added to the faction list, which introduces loyalist forces where the entry previously showed traitors only. Timeline 008.M31 retained, no source gives a firm year for Dwell.

entries.title: THE LAST REMEMBRANCER
entries.notes: Previous blurb described an anonymous remembrancer trying to chronicle the war. The actual story names Solomon Voss and is really about Rogal Dorn, with Iacton Qruze present as a Knight-Errant serving Malcador. Imperial Fists and Knights-Errant added alongside Remembrancers. Timeline 009.M31 retained but unverified: the only firm anchor is that Qruze is already a Knight-Errant, which places it after the Isstvan III survivors reach Terra.

entries.title: THE DEVINE ADORATRICE
entries.notes: Title in the manifest was wrong: the anthology contents list and the story's own page both give 'The Devine Adoratrice'. Devine is the ruling family surname on Molech, not the adjective 'divine'. The manifest's Thousand Sons attribution and sorcery blurb were pure invention: no Legion appears at all. This is a court-intrigue prequel to McNeill's Vengeful Spirit featuring House Devine, an Imperial Knights household, and the Sacristans who serve them. Lexicanum states the setting explicitly as 'Molech, 966.M30, the One hundred and Sixty-Eighth Year of the Great Crusade', which matches the manifest date, so the timeline is confirmed. 'Imperial Knights' is not currently in the site's faction vocabulary and would need adding; it matches neither the loyalist nor traitor filter, which is correct here.

entries.title: VIRTUES OF THE SONS
entries.notes: Plot and cast confirmed from the Lexicanum article and the quoted Black Library cover description. Emperor's Children and World Eaters were missing from the manifest's factions. Originally released as an Andy Smillie audio drama and later as prose; it appears in War Without End as a short story, so the type is unchanged. The date could not be sourced: the story is clearly Great Crusade era (Sanguinius consults Horus, joint Legion compliance actions), and the manifest's 001.M31 falls inside that window, so it has been left alone rather than replaced with a guess.

entries.title: SERMON OF EXODUS
entries.notes: Weakest entry in the batch. No plot summary exists on Lexicanum, Track of Words or any other source I could reach; the only real evidence is the Black Library cover line quoted on Lexicanum, 'Journeying from across the wastes of Davin, the faithful flock to prove themselves worthy in the eyes of dark gods. A Prequel to The Damnation of Pythos.' The blurb above says no more than that source supports. The manifest's Word Bearers attribution is not supported: nothing indicates the XVII Legion appears, and the Damnation of Pythos dramatis personae lists Iron Hands, Salamanders, Raven Guard, Emperor's Children and human colonists, not Word Bearers, so I have set the faction to 'Various' rather than assert a Legion. Timeline unverified and left at the manifest value: as a direct prequel to The Damnation of Pythos (007.M31 in this dataset) it probably belongs later than 004.M31, but I found nothing to pin it down and did not want to swap one guess for another.

entries.title: HOWL OF THE HEARTHWORLD
entries.notes: The manifest blurb was invented: the Space Wolves are not defending Fenris and there is no attack on their home world. This is a watch-pack story set en route to Terra. Faction and date left as they were: Space Wolves is correct, and 004.M31 sits sensibly against the site's own placement of Prospero Burns at 004-005.M31.

entries.title: LORD OF THE RED SANDS
entries.notes: Faction and date confirmed. Date matches the site's own placement of Galaxy in Flames and the Isstvan III atrocity at 005.M31. The manifest blurb was a reasonable guess but wrong in emphasis: this is not a flashback to Angron's gladiator past, it is the Isstvan III massacre from his point of view, ending on his answer about freedom. Also collected in the Angron anthology, The Imperial Truth and Crusade's End.

entries.title: ARTEFACTS
entries.notes: Faction and date confirmed: Salamanders, on Nocturne, immediately before the Dropsite Massacre, which this site places at 006.M31. The manifest blurb ('recover precious relics from the war's devastation') is the opposite of the plot, which is about destroying artefacts rather than recovering them, and is the origin of the Forgefather title and the seven relics of Nocturne. Confirms the audit note: Artefacts is also reprinted in Born of Flame, and additionally in Sedition's Gate (first publication) and Lupercal's War.

entries.title: CHIRURGEON
entries.notes: Faction confirmed. The manifest blurb ('experiments on the fallen', 'the Clonelord') was invented and also anachronistic: 'Clonelord' is a much later 41st-millennium epithet. No in-universe date could be sourced for this one; the manifest's 006.M31 is unverified but not demonstrably wrong, so it has been left alone. Note the story is largely flashback to the pre-Fulgrim III Legion.

entries.title: THE PHOENICIAN
entries.notes: Confirms the audit flag. The point-of-view character is Gabriel Santar of the Iron Hands, not an Emperor's Children protagonist, so Iron Hands has been added as the lead faction. Setting is Isstvan V, which this site dates 006.M31, matching the manifest. The manifest blurb was a generic 'Fulgrim's corruption' guess.

entries.title: ALLEGIANCE
entries.notes: Not a story about the White Scars picking a side in the civil war, as the manifest blurb claimed. It is Revuel Arvida's story, set immediately after Scars, so Thousand Sons has been added. The oath-breaker trials are of White Scars who swore to Horus, and the Khan's judgement is already made, not pending. Date left as the manifest range: the story opens right after the second battle of Prospero (007.M31 here) and covers a period of recovery, so 007-009.M31 is defensible, though 007.M31 alone would arguably be tighter.

entries.title: DAEMONOLOGY
entries.notes: Serious faction error in the manifest: this is a Mortarion and Death Guard story, not Thousand Sons. The title misled whoever wrote the original entry. Lexicanum gives the date explicitly, 'Mortarion brings his forces to the library-world Terathalion in 007.M31', which matches the manifest, so the timeline is confirmed. Thousand Sons are referenced only as the Legion that once brought Terathalion into compliance.

entries.title: GUNSIGHT
entries.notes: 'Various' replaced with the actual factions. This is a direct sequel to Swallow's novel Nemesis, following its surviving Vindicare, Eristede Kell, aboard the Sons of Horus flagship. Date unverified but consistent: this site places Nemesis at 007.M31 and the story happens years after Dagonet, so the manifest's 008.M31 is left as is. Lexicanum also files it under Sources (Black Legion) for the ending.

entries.title: THE LAUREL OF DEFIANCE
entries.notes: 'Various' replaced with Ultramarines. This is an Imperium Secundus political piece, not a generic last-stand story as the manifest blurb implied. Date left at 009.M31, consistent with this site's placement of The Unremembered Empire. Plot detail comes from the Black Library cover description quoted on Lexicanum; no fuller synopsis exists there, so the blurb stays within what that source states.

entries.title: A SAFE AND SHADOWED PLACE
entries.notes: 'Various' replaced. Direct prequel to the novel Pharos, introducing Skraivok and Krukesh. Ultramarines are included because the story turns on Sotha, the Pharos and Macragge, though the point of view is entirely Night Lords. Date left at 009.M31, matching this site's placement of Pharos.

entries.title: IMPERFECT
entries.notes: Faction left as Emperor's Children. Lexicanum also files it under Sources (Iron Hands), but the only Iron Hands presence is a Fabius-grown clone, so adding Iron Hands would wrongly flip the loyalist filter and I have left it off. The manifest blurb was a title paraphrase about the pursuit of perfection. Date unverified; the manifest's 009.M31 sits after Fulgrim's ascension at Iydris (007.M31 here) and is plausible, so left unchanged.

entries.title: WOLF MOTHER
entries.notes: Serious faction error in the manifest: nothing to do with the Space Wolves or Fenrisian tradition. The 'Wolf' of the title is Severian, a former Luna Wolf now serving Malcador as a Knight-Errant. Protagonist is Alivia Sureka, a Perpetual. Both 'Knights-Errant' and 'Perpetuals' are already in the site's faction vocabulary. Date left at 009.M31, immediately after Vengeful Spirit (008-009.M31 here), which the story follows directly.

entries.title: THE HARROWING
entries.notes: Confirms the audit flag: this is an Alpha Legion infiltration, not a generic survival-horror piece. 'Various' replaced with Alpha Legion and Mechanicum, which fixes a traitor-filter miss. Note Lexicanum has a separate page for a 41st-millennium Khornate warband also called The Harrowing, which is unrelated. Date unverified; manifest 009.M31 left unchanged.

entries.title: ALL THAT REMAINS
entries.notes: 'Various' replaced with Imperial Army, which the Black Library cover description names explicitly. No synopsis exists on Lexicanum and I found no other reliable source, so the blurb deliberately stops where the publisher's own description stops and does not state what the soldiers find or who they are. No named characters could be established, hence the empty mainCharacters array. Date unverified; manifest 009.M31 left unchanged.

entries.title: BY THE LION'S COMMAND
entries.notes: Death Guard added: they are the quarry throughout. The manifest blurb ('follow their Primarch's orders without question', 'absolute obedience') inverts the actual tension, which is Corswain acting alone, far from the Lion, on a decision the Lion has not made for him. Plot from the Black Library cover description; Lexicanum carries no fuller synopsis. Date unverified; 009.M31 is consistent with this site's placement of The Unremembered Empire and has been left.

entries.title: BLACK OCULUS
entries.notes: 'Various' replaced with Iron Warriors, fixing another traitor-filter miss. Not a void-battle story: it is a first-person Navigator monologue bridging Angel Exterminatus and the Battle of Tallarn. No named character exists for the narrator, so mainCharacters uses a descriptive label. Date left at the manifest range, which brackets this site's Tallarn entry at 010-012.M31.

entries.title: TWISTED
entries.notes: Confirms the audit flag: this is a Maloghurst story, and 'Twisted' is his epithet, not a description of corruption in general. 'Various' replaced with Sons of Horus, fixing a traitor-filter miss. Date unverified; manifest 010.M31 left unchanged.

entries.title: HANDS OF THE EMPEROR
entries.notes: Confirms the audit flag: the conflict is loyalist on loyalist, Custodian Guard against Imperial Fists over Terra, not Custodians striking at traitors as the manifest blurb said. Imperial Fists added. Plot from the Black Library cover description; Lexicanum has no fuller synopsis. Date unverified; manifest 012.M31 left unchanged, though the story could plausibly sit anywhere in the Palace fortification period.
